Contribuer à la modernisation progressive du portefeuille applicatif en remplaçant les applications arrivées en fin de vie, d’autres projets de refonte devant suivre. Coordonner les activités avec les prestataires internes et externes concernant les intégrations, la mise à disposition des environnements et les transferts de responsabilité. Exploitation, gestion des connaissances et amélioration continue Participer à l’exploitation des services numériques du SIRP conformément aux procédures documentées, notamment les mises en production planifiées, les mises à jour mensuelles des données et contenus applicatifs, les campagnes annuelles de collecte d’informations et de documents relatifs aux pensions, ainsi que le traitement des demandes de support utilisateurs. Améliorer et automatiser en permanence ces procédures opérationnelles afin de renforcer la fiabilité, la reproductibilité et la résilience des services. Mettre en place et maintenir l’infrastructure de gestion des connaissances de l’équipe, notamment les normes documentaires, une base de connaissances centralisée, les procédures d’exploitation et les parcours d’intégration, afin de garantir la traçabilité, la continuité des services et la polyvalence des équipes. Définir, mesurer et communiquer les indicateurs clés de performance des services et produits, et préparer des analyses et présentations à l’appui du reporting et de la prise de décision. Identifier et proposer des améliorations des processus et des outils, et promouvoir les bonnes pratiques communes au sein des activités informatiques du Service afin de favoriser une culture d’apprentissage continu et de partage des connaissances. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Formation Diplôme universitaire en informatique, technologies de l’information, interaction humain-machine ou dans une discipline étroitement liée, ou expérience professionnelle équivalente démontrant une expertise dans le domaine. Expérience professionnelle Au moins trois années d’expérience professionnelle confirmée dans le développement, le déploiement et l’exploitation d’applications web en production, idéalement dans un rôle orienté produit. Expérience démontrée dans l’animation des activités de découverte produit avec des parties prenantes non techniques ainsi que dans la rédaction de spécifications fonctionnelles et de critères d’acceptation jusqu’à leur validation. Expérience dans la conception d’interfaces accessibles et centrées sur l’utilisateur, avec une bonne connaissance du prototypage et des méthodes de recherche utilisateur. Expérience démontrée dans la mise en place ou la gestion de pratiques documentaires et de gestion des connaissances, notamment de bases de connaissances, de standards documentaires et de supports d’intégration, appuyée par d’excellentes compétences rédactionnelles. Une expérience dans l’analyse de systèmes hérités afin de reconstituer les règles métier et spécifier leur remplacement constituerait un avantage. Une expérience dans un environnement international et multiculturel serait appréciée. Outils et technologies Excellente maîtrise de TypeScript et React, avec une expérience de production sur Next.js ou un framework React comparable, ainsi qu’une bonne connaissance du développement back-end Node.js, des API REST et des bases de données relationnelles telles que PostgreSQL ou MySQL. item.title: E T Consultant
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, www.worldbank.org E astern and Southern Africa Regional Context The Eastern and Southern Africa (AFE) region is diverse, spanning low-income and lower-middle-income countries and a number of upper-middle-income borrowers, with wide variation in health outcomes, fiscal space, and institutional capacity. Many countries face a high and evolving burden of disease alongside persistent inequities in access and quality, while also managing recurrent shocks, including climate-related hazards, epidemics, and food and fuel price volatility. In this context, the World Bank supports governments through analytics, policy dialogue, and financing to strengthen human capital and build more resilient health systems and essential public health functions. Through its Health, Nutrition, and Population (HNP) Global Practice, the World Bank supports countries’ efforts towards achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and providing quality, affordable, equity-focused health services to everyone regardless of their ability to pay by strengthening primary health care systems and reducing the financial risks associated with ill-health. Some of the ongoing health and nutrition challenges in the AFE region include: • Triple burden of disease and epidemiological transition: a continuing burden of communicable diseases (including HIV, TB, malaria and outbreaks), persistently high maternal, newborn and child mortality in many settings, and a rapidly growing burden of NCDs and injuries—often coexisting within the same populations and health systems. • Health system constraints and inequities: persistent gaps in access to quality essential services, especially for rural, remote, and vulnerable populations, driven by constraints in the health workforce, medicines and supply chains, service readiness, governance and accountability, and limited fiscal space and financial protection for households. • Nutrition and food insecurity: high levels of child stunting and micronutrient deficiencies in several countries, alongside rising overweight/obesity, compounded by food price shocks and climate variability that affect diets and worsen vulnerability throughout the life course. Summary of Botswana and Southern Africa Health Portfolio The World Bank’s health portfolio in Botswana combines investment financing with targeted technical assistance (TA) and analytics to advance the Government’s priorities on UHC, primary health care revitalization, and health security. The portfolio is anchored by the Botswana Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (HEPRR) Project, which supports preparedness and response; strengthened surveillance, laboratory, and emergency management systems; and investments in core enablers, including digital public health infrastructure and availability of quality data. In parallel, the World Bank provides TA supporting sector planning and governance such as development of the Health Sector Strategic Plan, digital health and data use (interoperability, registries, and routine data quality and use), and improvements in supply chain performance and regulatory systems for health products. This work is complemented by analytics to inform reforms and investments, including on health financing and efficiency, equity, and service delivery performance to strengthen human capital and system resilience. Across southern Africa, the World Bank’s health engagement in South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho combines investment lending with analytical and advisory services to strengthen primary health care, improve quality of care, and build more resilient health systems. In Lesotho, the portfolio includes an active health and nutrition system strengthening project focused on expanding coverage and improving the quality of essential maternal and child health, nutrition, and NCD services, alongside reforms to strengthen stewardship and service delivery readiness. There are opportunities to support the preparation of new operations and enhance the scope of TA and advisory work in southern Africa. In South Africa and Namibia, support is anchored in policy dialogue and analytics, including public expenditure and efficiency work, to inform reforms that expand effective coverage, reduce inequities, and improve the sustainability of health financing. Objectives and Scope of Work In light of the growing health portfolio, the HAEH2 team seeks an Extended-Term Consultant (ETC) with experience as a Health Specialist/Economist to provide day-to-day technical and operational support to HNP task teams and Government counterparts, primarily in Botswana and, as needed, across the southern Africa portfolio. The scope of work includes: • Provide technical and operational support to the health portfolio in Botswana. The ETC will support implementation of the Botswana health portfolio (including the HEPRR project) by monitoring progress against the results framework (including support to M E, data quality, and results reporting) and follow-up on agreed actions; supporting planning and delivery of implementation support missions; and contributing to key operational deliverables (aide memoires, management briefs, and client-facing communications). The ETC will help convene consultations with the Ministry of Health and other stakeholders, monitor progress, and coordinate with fiduciary, safeguards, and technical colleagues to ensure timely, integrated support. • Help ensure close coordination with government, development partners, and the CMU and World Bank teams across other sectors in Botswana. The ETC will facilitate coordination and information flow across the Ministry of Health and other relevant agencies, development partners, and World Bank teams (including the Country Management Unit and colleagues in other sectors) to align priorities, timelines, and implementation support. The ETC will play a pivotal role in providing strategic sectoral guidance to the CMU and provide key inputs into country management reviews and documents. • Support policy dialogue with the Ministry of Health, relevant national institutions, and other stakeholders. The ETC will support policy dialogue by preparing briefs, talking points, and presentations, synthesizing implementation experience, sector analytics, and international lessons. The ETC will help translate discussions into clear decisions and follow-up actions to inform priority reforms in primary health care, health security, health financing, and other system strengthening areas. • Provide technical and operational support to the health portfolio in southern Africa, as needed. The ETC will support task teams in South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho, including assistance with preparation and follow-up of missions and key deliverables, and contributions to selected analytical and advisory work (e.g., service delivery performance, health financing and efficiency, and health security). Duties and Accountabilities: The ETC’s key tasks and activities will include but are not limited to: • Support implementation support for HEPRR and other Botswana portfolio activities, including monitoring implementation and results; consolidating inputs across technical, fiduciary and ESF colleagues; and proactively following up with counterparts on agreed actions. • Contribute to the planning, preparation, and follow-up of missions, technical consultations, and key portfolio engagements, including drafting agenda/talking points, preparing briefing packages, and drafting aide memoires and progress reports, and management updates as requested by Task Team Leaders. • Support monitoring and evaluation (M E) and results reporting for the portfolio, including maintaining an M E implementation plan, supporting updates to the results framework and indicator definitions as needed, compiling and quality-checking data and narrative inputs for progress reporting. • Provide technical inputs to project implementation, including review of technical specifications and Terms of References for goods and services (e.g., medical and laboratory equipment, digital systems, and technical assistance), and advise on alignment with good practice, user requirements, and World Bank procurement principles (in coordination with procurement specialists). • Support stakeholder coordination across Government, development partners, and World Bank teams (including the CMU and other sectors) by preparing coordination notes, documenting decisions, and escalating issues requiring management attention. • Contribute to selected analytical and advisory activities (ASA), including literature and data review, drafting sections of technical notes and reports, and supporting quality assurance to ensure analytical rigor and consistency of messaging. • As needed, provide operational and analytical support to the southern Africa health portfolio (South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho). • Maintain well-organized records of key documents and correspondence; support timely sharing of information within task teams; and contribute to knowledge management by capturing lessons learned and good practices.

item.title: Economist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Visit https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/home Global practice for Fiscal Policy and Growth (FPG) The Fiscal Policy and Growth (FPG) Department leads the World Bank Group’s policy dialogue and engagement with countries to strengthen macro-fiscal foundations, including debt sustainability, debt management, public expenditure, and domestic resource mobilization, trade and investment and to accelerate job creation and inclusive growth. FPG links the macroeconomic dialogue with programs focused on expanding the role of the private sector in economic development. In its day-to-day engagement, FPG supports Ministries of Finance, Planning, Economy, Industry and Trade, and Production in pursuing reform agendas that strengthen job creation through inclusive, private sector-led growth. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/topic/fiscal-policy-and-growth Background and general description The FPG unit for Southern Africa and East Africa (EAEM2) is looking for a local economist to be based in Maputo, Mozambique. The selected candidate will contribute substantially to analytical work and lending operations. She or he will report to the FPG Practice Manager covering the EAEM2 unit, which comprises 14 countries across three Country Management Units: AECS1 (South Africa, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia), AECS2 (Mozambique, Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, Seychelles), and AECC2 (Angola, Democratic Republic of Congo, São Tomé and Príncipe, and Burundi). The unit has a strong focus on prudent macro-fiscal policies, structural reforms, inclusive growth, and job creation. The World Bank’s FPG engagement in Mozambique supports the country’s efforts to strengthen macroeconomic stability, fiscal and debt sustainability, domestic resource mobilization, and the management of natural-resource revenues, while fostering a more diversified, productive, and job-rich economy. The work program combines policy dialogue, financing operations, technical assistance, and analytical work, including macroeconomic monitoring, Macro Poverty Outlooks, economic updates, public finance analysis, and work on growth and jobs. Particular attention is given to translating Mozambique’s natural-resource potential into broad-based development outcomes, strengthening institutions and fiscal frameworks, and supporting private-sector development and economic resilience. As an Economist for EAEM2, you will contribute to the country team covering Mozambique and, as needed, to the regional FPG team working on other countries. The Economist will be based in Maputo and work closely with the Division Director, Senior Country Economist, Lead Economist, and other members of the country team, and will report to the FPG Practice Manager. The position requires strong analytical capability, sound judgment, close engagement with government counterparts and development partners, and the ability to deliver high-quality outputs under tight deadlines. The Country Economist will: • Contribute to FPG Advisory Services and Analytics (ASA) in macroeconomic and fiscal management, macroeconomic modelling, data analysis, public finance, growth, jobs, and private-sector development; • Collect, analyze, validate, and maintain economic, fiscal, debt, external-sector, financial, and socioeconomic data related to Mozambique, and communicate findings clearly through tables, charts, briefs, presentations, and analytical notes; • Maintain macroeconomic databases and regularly prepare updated medium-term macroeconomic projections, using economic and financial models and World Bank toolkits; • Contribute to the preparation of Macro Poverty Outlooks, economic updates, public finance and growth diagnostics, Debt Sustainability Analysis, Country Policy and Institutional Assessments, policy notes, and other country and regional knowledge products; • Contribute to the design and implementation of financing operations, including Development Policy Financing, to the design and implementation of SDFP Performance and Policy Actions, and to technical assistance supporting the Government’s reform program; • Serve as a task leader or team member for country-specific financing operations and/or analytical and advisory services, commensurate with experience; • Support the Country Management Unit in implementing the World Bank program in Mozambique and contribute to cross-practice collaboration around country priorities; • Contribute to policy dialogue with government counterparts on macro-fiscal policy, debt, domestic revenue mobilization, natural-resource revenue management, structural transformation, productivity, and job creation; • Establish and strengthen partnerships with bilateral and multilateral agencies, research institutions, academia, civil society, and other stakeholders, helping leverage knowledge and resources; • Contribute to the dissemination of World Bank knowledge products to government, development partners, civil society, academia, the private sector, and other key audiences; and • Contribute to regional and cross-country analytical and operational work within EAEM2 as business needs require.

item.title: Senior Water Specialist, Governance and Regulation
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . The WBG Planet Vice Presidency is leading WBG’s efforts to make the planet livable, as a necessary condition for job creation and poverty elimination. It is responsible for getting the right public and private sector solutions to our operational teams and to our clients, and to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact and business to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs, focusing on agribusiness, tourism (nature-based tourism), infrastructure (water) and health (sanitation, nutrition); supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, policy environment, and private sector mobilization; and supporting and accelerating specific targets and commitments such as Mission AgriConnect, Mission Water, Climate Change Action Plan. The VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. WBG Water Department - Water for People, Food, and Planet. The World Bank Group’s Water Strategy Implementation Plan (WSIP) translates ambition into operational action. Water security is not only about access. It is a foundation of resilient and prosperous societies where sustained water resources, reliable services, and risk management underpin growth, human development, jobs, and livelihoods. Approved in December 2025, the WSIP sets a collective target to improve water security for 400 million people by 2030 and organizes delivery through three outcome pillars: Water for People, Water for Food, and Water for Planet. Delivery is enabled by scalable solutions, knowledge for impact at scale, and programmatic approaches and partnerships. The WBG Water Department works with regions to implement the WSIP through solutions tailored to key client segments, including national and sub-national governments, private sector operators, investors, and financial institutions. Implementation is organized around three core delivery mechanisms: (i) country-led Water Compacts that deploy WBG resources in countries committed to policy and regulatory actions; (ii) coordinated public and private interventions to mobilize capital investments; and (iii) multiphase programmatic approaches that replicate and scale what works. The WBG is also expanding collaboration with partners, including MDBs and philanthropies, through Mission Water to accelerate global water security and reach many more people in developing countries. This agenda is reinforced by the World Bank Group’s shift toward a more integrated Knowledge Bank that shortens the distance from insight to implementation. In Water, the Knowledge Bank delivery model is structured into two global units that translate knowledge into impact at scale: • Policy and Regulations Unit: Provides global thought leadership and evidence-based policy support to advance water security for people, food, and the planet. It supports regional teams in strengthening water sector governance, in particular on policies, institutions and regulations (PIR), including supporting an enabling environment for private finance. The team will help ensure the WBG’s leadership in global water and development discourse through evidence-based analytics and hands-on support. The unit drives innovation and knowledge management by advancing research and leading water data and analytics for policymaking. It also supports regional task teams to meet the highest standards on inclusion, climate resilient design, and dam safety. • Solutions and Impact Unit: Scales and replicates high-impact water projects and innovations across WBG operations to deliver results for people, food, and the planet. The Unit leads the consolidation and rollout of scalable water solutions, supports regional teams to accelerate implementation of the WSIP, and provides operational support and portfolio oversight. It drives impact through robust monitoring and evaluation, knowledge sharing, and applied research, while helping country teams adapt global solutions to local contexts and political economy realities. These global units operate within the WBG Water Department’s leadership structure alongside Global Leads for the three WSIP outcome pillars and cross-cutting areas such as Financing, Governance and Regulation, and Water for Prosperity. Together, they enable a governance and regulation anchored delivery approach that strengthens institutions, improves accountability and performance, and creates the enabling conditions for investment and sustainable service delivery at scale. The WBG Water Department is comprised of 65 staff. Senior Water Specialist, Governance and Regulation: The Senior Water Specialist, Governance and Regulation, will report to the WBG Manager, Policy and Regulations, who is accountable to the WBG Director, Water. Key responsibilities: The Senior Water Specialist, Governance and Regulation, will be responsible for leading on water sector policies, institutions and regulatory (PIR) support to WBG internal and external clients of the WBG Water Global Leadership Team, and being a thought-leader in this space. Specific duties and accountabilities include the following: 1. Provide just-in-time strategic and hands-on advice and guidance on water sector regulatory issues, based on global lessons learned and fit-for-purpose solutions for the respective country/client context, following-through on support to help lead to tangible results for WBG operations. 2. Provide just-in-time strategic and hands-on advice and guidance on appropriate policy and institutional issues, based on global lessons learned and fit-for-purpose solutions for the respective country/client context, following-through on support to help lead to tangible results for WBG operations. 3. Lead and/or contribute to sharp and concise operations-oriented research and analysis to bring the latest knowledge and innovation to our support to clients, collaborating with others, both inside and outside the Water Global Department, to ensure full synergies. 4. Lead and/or contribute to papers on PIR for water, blogs and other communication materials, and contribute to global flagship reports, curate lessons learned and case studies, participating in select conferences and events as agreed with management, and the like. 5. Participate in relevant corporate initiatives and undertake relevant corporate reviews to ensure WBG Global Water contributions reflect the latest and context-appropriate thinking that consider PIR in the water sector. 6. Provide briefings to senior management on complex PIR on an as-needed basis. 7. Be an active participant of the Water Global Department’s Leadership Team and specifically the P R Unit’s Leadership Team. 8. Work with management to develop a core team of PIR experts to provide hands-on support to task teams on PIR, within existing budgetary and other parameters. 9. Participate in all relevant activities sponsored by the Global Water Security and Sanitation Partnership to support and inform WBG Water Global partners. 10. Other related tasks.

item.title: Procurement Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank consists of two entities – the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). It is a global development cooperative owned by 189 member countries. As the largest development bank in the world, the World Bank provides loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and coordinates responses to regional and global challenges. Visit http://www.worldbank.org/ Regional and Country Context Countries of the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan (MENAAP) region confront a vast array of development challenges, from an uncertain and uneven recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic to the implications of decelerating global economy, deepening geopolitical divisions, protracted regional conflicts, and climate change. These overlapping crises are amplified by longstanding structural relating to economic governance that contribute to an outsized presence of the state in the economy, high unemployment rates among women and youth, and limited intraregional trade and investment. Overcoming these challenges will allow MENAAP countries to realize their vast development potential, endowed as the region is with a rapidly growing and highly educated population, geo-strategic location, and abundance of renewable energy potential. To unlock this potential, the World Bank is advancing inclusive, sustainable, and resilient development through a two-pronged strategy that seeks to respond to sudden and severe crises while supporting reforms that spur structural transformation and job creation, advance gender equity, strengthen regional cooperation, and accelerate green transitions. This strategy is operationalized through a differentiated approach that reflects the distinct circumstances of the World Bank’s clients in the region, comprising 22 countries that range from active IBRD borrowers and IDA recipients to recipients of reimbursable advisory services and non-active countries with whom the Bank maintains a policy dialogue. For more on the World Bank in MENAAP, visit www.worldbank.org/en/region/mena . The World Bank’s MENAAP region consists primarily of the Front Office of the Regional Vice President, the Chief Economist, 7 Country Management Units, 4 Regional Directorships, and close linkages with Human resources (HR), Resource Management, and Corporate Security. The Country Management Unit (CMU-MAP07) engagement in Pakistan is through a combination of lending and technical assistance. The MAP07 is headed by a director and an operation manager both based in Islamabad, Pakistan. The current Pakistan portfolio includes 53 active projects with the total financing commitment from IDA and IBRD of about US$ 16.4 billion. The projects are implemented at both the federal and provincial levels. Procurement The Prosperity Vice Presidency is one of the World Bank Group’s five verticals, with a mandate that emphasizes “Growth, Finance, and Institutions for all.” Our approach leverages data-driven analysis and combines expertise from both the public and private sectors, together with International Finance Corporation (IFC). The Prosperity Vice Presidency supports clients in advancing evidence-based structural reforms to establish the foundations for inclusive and sustainable growth in the thematic areas of macro-fiscal policy; financial sector resilience, access, and deepening; private sector development, trade, and competitiveness; and governance and public sector reform, including statistical capacity. Prosperity is comprised of five Global Departments. EMAPR is under the authority of a Procurement Manager for MENAAP who directly reports to the MENAAP Prosperity Regional Practice Director. Most MENAAP Procurement staff members are decentralized through the establishment of procurement teams in Country Offices (COs) including in: Pakistan, Afghanistan, Egypt, Lebanon, Morocco, Tunisia, Djibouti, Iraq, Jordan and the West Bank and Gaza. All procurement staff members are managed by Accredited Practice Manager (APM), who is based at the World Bank Cairo, Egypt office. Responsibilities: The Procurement Specialist will help support and further develop the CMU’s work program in Pakistan. He/she will participate and play a key role in the operational, analytical, and advisory activities of the unit. This requires strong knowledge of both economic and public-sector governance issues, as well as extensive experience in operations. He/she will also have diplomatic skills to engage effectively with the many stakeholders involved inside and outside the Bank. He/she will have demonstrated ability to work effectively with counterparts in government as well as with multilateral and bilateral institutions. He/she is also expected to establish and maintain good working relationships with a variety of international and national partner organizations (academia, civil society groups, local research centers). He/she will work with a team comprising 5 Senior, 1 Procurement Specialists and 1 procurement analyst based in Islamabad and Karachi, Pakistan, and a Hub Leader based in Islamabad, Pakistan. The selected candidate will undertake the following tasks: • Works independently under general direction of the Hub leader and procurement manager. Organizes and delivers procurement services at the CMU. He/She should ensure appropriate fiduciary and quality controls, and consistent application and interpretation of policy in making procurement decisions. • Independently, organizes and conducts reviews of procurement aspects of Bank documents, including Project Appraisal Documents, Legal Agreements, Quality Enhancement Review Documents, Development Policy Lending (DPL), Fiduciary Assessments and Board Papers that require procurement input and prepares a range of procurement-related documents and reports. • Contributes together with other procurement colleagues and under the guidance of the APM ensures consistency in the procurement approach across the region. • Provides technical fiduciary advice on procurement activities and engages in policy dialogue to strengthen procurement systems. • Supports clients in achieving value for money in public procurement to enhance service delivery and development outcomes with integrity. • Understand relevant procurement markets using analytical tools and approaches to define more effective procurement strategies. • Participates in missions and plays a key role in developing practical approaches to procurement while simultaneously dealing with policy and operational issues. • Prepares and/or comments on draft operational directives and policy papers; produces high quality procurement reports. • Develops and executes training modules on sector related procurement topics. • Help clients to develop PPSDs (Project Procurement Strategy for Development), conducts Fiduciary Assessments for PforRs, keep the procurement portfolio up to date, with PRAMs and PPRs conducted with quality and timely. Review, clear and contribute to the improvement of the quality of procurement documents. • Ensures the use of electronic tools, e.g., Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP) to track exchanges with the clients and performance of key fiduciary metrics covering the operations portfolio, as well as the unit's own work program deliverables. • Designs and delivers capacity building workshops for Bank staff, private sector and Borrowers staff. • Provide Hands-on Expanded Implementation Support (HEIS) when requested by the APM in Pakistan or any of the countries in the region.

item.title: Associate Data Engineer, Enterprise Data Engineering
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 130 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org ITS Vice Presidency Context: The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Unit Context: The ITS Data Office (ITSDO) is the central entity within the World Bank Group’s Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) department responsible for enabling data, AI, information, and knowledge capabilities across the institution. It comprises four Units focused on platforms tools, product service delivery, enablement and governance. The office plays a pivotal role in advancing the Bank’s digital transformation, supporting business domains with trusted data, information and AI capabilities, and fostering a culture of responsible innovation. The Platforms Tools Unit is responsible for building, integrating, and continuously modernizing the foundational technology infrastructure that powers data, AI, archives, and knowledge services across the World Bank Group. The unit leads the rationalization and simplification of legacy systems, and modernization towards platforms that are scalable, secure, interoperable, and designed for self-service and adoption. The unit plays a critical role in enabling enterprise-wide transformation by delivering data environments, digitization infrastructure, and open knowledge repositories that are AI-ready and aligned with business needs. Duties and accountabilities: Data Pipeline Development • Design, develop, and maintain data pipelines for ingestion, transformation, and serving across batch and streaming workloads • Build ETL/ELT workflows to integrate data from diverse sources into enterprise data platforms • Build document ingestion and processing pipelines incorporating OCR, metadata extraction, content enrichment, classification, and indexing capabilities. • Develop data transformation logic using Apache Spark, PySpark, SparkSQL, and SQL • Implement change data capture (CDC) patterns for real-time and near-real-time data synchronization • Build streaming data pipelines for real-time analytics and operational use cases • Optimize pipeline performance, resource utilization, and cost efficiency Federated Data Pipelines Domain Enablement • Support federated data pipeline architecture that enables Line of Business (LOB) teams to own and manage their domain data • Contribute to self-serve data infrastructure that abstracts complexity and allows domain teams to build pipelines independently • Develop standardized pipeline deployment patterns that LOB teams can adopt while maintaining autonomy • Support domain teams in building data products that are discoverable, interoperable, and compliant with enterprise standards • Support domain teams in creating and managing structured and unstructured data products, ensuring metadata, discoverability, and interoperability across enterprise platforms. • Enable distributed data processing across domains while ensuring consistency through federated governance • Assist in establishing data contracts and interoperability standards that allow seamless data sharing across domains • Support the balance between domain autonomy and enterprise-wide governance requirements Templates, Blueprints Patterns • Develop reusable pipeline templates and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) patterns for common data product types • Create blueprints for data ingestion, transformation, quality validation, and serving that LOB teams can customize • Build standardized patterns for batch pipelines, streaming pipelines, CDC implementations, and API-based integrations • Develop reusable patterns and accelerators for document ingestion, OCR, metadata extraction, content enrichment, and indexing of unstructured content • Contribute to a pattern library covering medallion architecture, dimensional modeling, and data product packaging • Document best practices and reference architectures that guide LOB teams in building compliant, high-quality pipelines • Develop starter kits and accelerators that reduce time-to-value for domain teams building new data products • Create cookbooks and implementation guides that translate enterprise standards into actionable steps • Support LOB teams in adopting templates while allowing appropriate customization for domain-specific needs Data Integration • Integrate data from multiple internal and external sources into unified data assets • Build reusable data integration patterns and connectors for enterprise data sources • Implement data ingestion using Auto Loader, COPY INTO, and other ingestion frameworks • Develop API-based data integrations and file-based data processing workflows • Ensure data consistency and reliability across integrated sources • Support data migration efforts and legacy system integrations Data Modeling Transformation • Implement medallion architecture patterns (bronze, silver, gold) for data organization and quality progression • Develop dimensional models, fact tables, and aggregations for analytics use cases • Build data transformation logic that ensures accuracy, consistency, and business alignment • Create reusable transformation components and modular pipeline designs • Optimize data models for query performance and consumption patterns • Support schema evolution and data versioning requirements Data Quality Testing • Implement data quality checks, validation rules, and automated testing within pipelines • Develop data profiling and anomaly detection to identify quality issues • Build data reconciliation processes to ensure accuracy across systems • Implement unit testing, integration testing, and regression testing for pipelines • Monitor data quality metrics and remediate issues proactively • Document data quality rules and thresholds for pipeline outputs Data Observability Operations • Implement logging, monitoring, and alerting for pipeline health and performance • Build dashboards to track pipeline execution, data freshness, and quality metrics • Develop automated error handling, retry logic, and failure notifications • Support incident response and troubleshooting for pipeline failures • Implement data lineage tracking to support auditability and impact analysis • Implement monitoring and observability for AI and data products, including pipeline health, data quality, and retrieval effectiveness. • Ensure pipelines meet SLAs for data availability and freshness Analytics AI Enablement • Build data pipelines that enable analytics, reporting, and business intelligence use cases • Build and maintain document processing pipelines for extraction, classification, chunking, enrichment, and indexing of unstructured content • Develop content chunking, metadata extraction, indexing, and enrichment workflows to support enterprise search and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions. • Prepare and serve data for machine learning and AI workloads • Develop feature engineering pipelines for ML model development • Create semantic layers and curated datasets that enable self-service analytics • Support integration with analytics tools including Power BI and Tableau • Build data products with clear documentation and consumption guidance Collaboration Enablement • Partner with data architects to align pipeline development with architectural standards • Collaborate with business analysts and data scientists to understand data requirements • Work with platform engineers to leverage platform capabilities effectively • Contribute to technical documentation, runbooks, and knowledge sharing • Contribute to platform standards, reusable frameworks, and engineering best practices for data and AI solutions • Support data consumers in understanding and accessing data assets • Participate in code reviews and follow engineering best practices

item.title: ET Consultant - Mining Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career with impact? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, please visit www.worldbank.org . Infrastructure Vice Presidency (INF VPU) The WBG Infrastructure Vice Presidency is responsible for getting the right public and private sector solutions for our operational teams and to our clients, and to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs; supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, policy environment, and private sector mobilization; focusing on agribusiness, healthcare, infrastructure, manufacturing, and tourism; and support and accelerate specific targets such as M300, Health 1.5bn, and SP 500. The VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/infrastructure Metals and Minerals Policy and Regulation Team (KIMPR) The global mining sector continues to evolve rapidly. Urbanization, agriculture, digitalization, and a soaring need for energy could double the demand for critical minerals by 2040. For many countries, meeting this demand presents a significant opportunity to create jobs and growth. Mining can generate substantial government revenue through taxes, royalties, and state equity stakes that fund schools, clinics, infrastructure, and digital services. With the right policies and safeguards, mining can progress from a purely extractive industry to one that includes manufacturing and processing. This progress ensures that value and jobs stay local with a long-lasting impact. The Metals and Minerals Policy and Regulation unit is embedded within the INF VPU’s Metals and Minerals Department of the World Bank Group. This global unit of technical experts is responsible for the design and implementation of World Bank operations and knowledge activities in mining a t both global and country levels. KIMPR works closely with a multi-donor trust fund program the Extractives Global Programmatic Support (EGPS) and KIMPR team manages global initiatives, including Coal Mines Closure – Just Transitions , and the Climate Smart Mining (CSM) , and the Resilient and Inclusive Supply Chain Enhancement (RISE) program. Within the Metals and Minerals Team, KIMPR also works closely with the Metals and Minerals Solutions and Impact team (KIMSI), which is responsible for ensuring that the right mix of best practice, investment and advisory solutions are made available to our clients and WBG operational teams in the Metals and Minerals sectors. The objective of the KIMPR Unit is to provide technical advice and support on cutting-edge policy, analytical work, and investment lending preparation for government clients, often resulting in financing to support developing countries transform their natural resource wealth into sustainable, resilient, and inclusive economic development, consistent with climate mitigation goals. NOTE : This position is financed by a Trust Fund and renewal is contingent upon availability of funding, in addition to other factors, including but not limited to business needs, staff performance and skills fit. Job Duties and Responsibilities: The selected candidate will be based in the World Bank’s office in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, contribute to the design and implementation of World Bank operations and knowledge activities supported by the EGPS program in metals and minerals sector and with primary focus on Uzbekistan (and possibly extending in the Central Asia region): I. Day-to-Day Liaison with Government Counterparts • Serve as the primary point of contact with key government counterparts in Uzbekistan, including the Ministry of Mining Industry and Geology, ensuring timely communication, follow-up on agreed actions, and continuity of engagement across workstreams. • Support the finalization and implementation of the Metals and Minerals Country Compact in Uzbekistan by facilitating coordination between government counterparts and WBG teams and tracking progress against agreed milestones. • Contribute to the development and refinement of national mining strategies, policies, or regulations, ensuring coherence with institutional capacities, implementation feasibility, and alignment with the country's broader critical minerals agenda. II. Internal Monitoring and Project Implementation • Assist in the monitoring and reporting of project implementation progress across the portfolio, including contributions to internal and external reporting tools and fiduciary requirements. • Support the implementation of project activities, missions and events, identifying emerging challenges and proposing adaptive measures in collaboration with relevant stakeholders. III. Stakeholder Engagement and Donor Coordination • Support policy dialogue and reform processes in the mining sector, engaging with government counterparts, development partners, and private sector actors across the region. • Provide technical support to the development of initiatives in collaboration with national and regional partners, including mapping of donor activities and identification of coordination and co-financing opportunities with partners such as the EBRD, ADB, and bilateral donors. • Support transparency and good governance initiatives in the extractive sector, including potential engagement with the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) process, multi-stakeholder dialogue mechanisms, and related efforts to strengthen revenue transparency, beneficial ownership disclosure, and accountable resource governance. IV. Analytical Work • Conduct analytical work that informs strategic planning along the critical minerals value chain — spanning exploration, mining, processing, and value addition — with a focus on key mining regions and territorial development considerations. • Contribute to the framing of the World Bank's strategy and service responses to evolving technical, fiscal, regulatory, environmental, and social challenges in the mineral sector. V. Advisory and Knowledge Sharing • Collaborate with WBG global and regional teams in developing mining sector and critical minerals value chain strategies, and support related policy advisory and knowledge exchange activities. • Provide technical input across thematic areas relevant to critical minerals value chains, including geology and exploration, permitting and licensing, transparency and governance, environmental and social standards, and downstream value addition. The position will work in close collaboration with the Metals and Minerals Solutions and Impact team (KIMSI), to ensure alignment with departmental priorities and the delivery of integrated, cross-cutting results. It will also strengthen the articulation between public sector engagement and private sector investments, supporting the development of bankable pipelines and investment-ready opportunities.

Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The OECD has earned a leading role in financial and business issues. The core mission of the Directorate for Financial and Enterprise Affairs ( DAF ) is to assist markets to fund inclusive economic growth, and in turn Better Lives, through setting and implementing standards, providing capacity building and technical assistance, acting as a forum for co-operation and collaboration across the OECD Directorates, external stakeholders and International Organisations. DAF's mission is pursued through five substantive divisions whose teams provide member and partner countries with policy guidance, analysis and support in the areas of competition, anti-corruption, corporate governance, financial markets, insurance and pensions, consumer finance, responsible business conduct and international investment. DAF currently employs about 300 staff members (economists, lawyers, statisticians, support staff, consultants, and trainees), who support work across a broad range of policy areas. The DAF/CM Division is looking for a Communications Officer to plan and conduct a wide range of communication tasks to enhance the relevance, visibility, and impact of the Division’s work on policymakers, stakeholders, and the general public. This includes working on publications, the web, traditional and social media, design, and events, in line with OECD corporate communications priorities, rules and best practices. The selected candidate will work under the supervision of CM’s head of communications and in close co-operation with the Communications Unit in the Director’s Office (DO) and the OECD Communications Directorate (COM). "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Publications Work with the Division’s analysts on preparing publications (reports, papers, policy briefs, etc.), advising them throughout the publishing process. Copyedit, format and proofread manuscripts to ensure clarity and consistency of messaging and applying all OECD style rules and conventions. Draft short materials (articles, blog posts, etc.) to promote publications. Promote publications through multiple channels (web, social media, events, etc.) and identify opportunities to increase visibility across platforms and audiences. Media Develop social media campaigns for key events (publication launches, etc.) and regularly draft content for various platforms (e.g. LinkedIn, X, WhatsApp) to promote outputs. Monitor social media to evaluate the impact of campaigns. Support work with traditional media, including in the preparation of materials (draft press releases, etc.) and monitoring of media coverage. Web Update and maintain CM web pages, following corporate web rules and best practices, and ensure maximum visibility and discoverability of information. Draft original web content and adapt texts for the web, following best practices for SEO and GEO. Design & multimedia Design high-quality communication materials targeted at a variety of stakeholders (e.g. flyers, brochures, videos, infographics). Propose new promotional approaches, aligned with corporate rules and tools, and keep abreast of best practices and innovations at the OECD and externally. Events Manage the communication needs of events (e.g. conferences, workshops, webinars), including through the development of dedicated websites or webpages, visual signatures following OECD branding rules, agendas, and other promotional activities. Strategic planning & Internal communications Contribute to DAF’s annual communications plan and ensure that CM communications activities support the delivery of this plan as well as the DAF Director’s communications priorities. Work collaboratively with the Division’s other Communications Officers and provide support and back-up when needed. Coordinate with the DAF DO Communications Unit and COM in planning communications activities. Support impact monitoring and knowledge-sharing within the Division to maximise outreach efforts and exchange best practices. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background Bachelor’s degree, preferably in communications, journalism or public affairs. Excellent innovation skills and attention to detail. Previous experience working in the financial sector would be an advantage. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. L'OCDE a acquis un rôle de premier plan sur les questions financières et commerciales. La mission principale de la Direction des affaires financières et des entreprises ( DAF ) est d'aider les marchés à financer une croissance économique inclusive et, par conséquent, une vie meilleure, en établissant et en mettant en œuvre des normes, en fournissant un renforcement des capacités et une assistance technique, et en servant de forum de coopération et de collaboration entre les directions de l'OCDE, les parties prenantes externes et les organisations internationales. La mission de la DAF s'exerce par l'intermédiaire de cinq divisions fonctionnelles dont les équipes fournissent aux pays membres et partenaires des orientations, des analyses et un soutien en matière de politiques publiques dans les domaines de la concurrence, de la lutte contre la corruption, de la gouvernance d'entreprise, des marchés financiers, des assurances et des retraites, du crédit à la consommation, de la conduite responsable des entreprises et de l'investissement international. La DAF emploie actuellement environ 350 personnes (économistes, juristes, statisticiens, personnel de soutien, consultants et stagiaires), qui contribuent à des travaux dans un large éventail de domaines politiques. La Division des marchés de capitaux et des institutions financières (CM) se concentre sur les domaines thématiques suivants : marchés financiers et économie financière, assurances et retraites, éducation financière et protection des consommateurs, gouvernance d’entreprise et entreprises publiques. Ces travaux sont menés sous la direction du Comité des marchés financiers et du Comité de gouvernance d’entreprise, et leurs sous-comités respectifs. La Division DAF/CM recherche un(e) chargé(e) de communication pour planifier et mener à bien un large éventail d'activités visant à renforcer la pertinence, la visibilité et l'impact des travaux de la Division auprès des décideurs, des parties prenantes et du grand public. Ces activités englobent notamment les publications, le web, les médias traditionnels et les réseaux sociaux, le graphisme ainsi que l'organisation d'événements conformément aux priorités, aux règles et aux meilleures pratiques de l'OCDE en matière de communication d'entreprise. Le/la candidat(e) retenu(e) travaillera sous la supervision du responsable de la communication de CM et en étroite collaboration avec l'unité de communication du Cabinet du Directeur (DO) ainsi qu'avec la Direction de la communication de l'OCDE (COM). "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Publications • Collaborer avec les analystes de la Division à l’élaboration de publications (rapports, documents d’analyse, notes d’orientation, etc.) et les conseiller tout au long du processus de publication. • Réviser, mettre en forme et relire les manuscrits afin de garantir la clarté et la cohérence du message et en appliquant toutes les règles et conventions de style de l'OCDE. • Rédiger des contenus courts (articles, billets de blog, etc.) pour promouvoir les publications. • Assurer la promotion des publications via divers canaux (Web, réseaux sociaux, événements, etc.) et identifier des opportunités d’accroître leur visibilité auprès de différents publics et sur diverses plateformes. Médias • Élaborer des campagnes sur les réseaux sociaux pour des événements clés (lancements de publications, etc.) et rédiger régulièrement du contenu pour diverses plateformes (par ex. LinkedIn, X, WhatsApp) afin de promouvoir les réalisations. • Assurer une veille sur les réseaux sociaux pour évaluer l'impact des campagnes. • Appuyer les relations avec les médias traditionnels, notamment en préparant des supports (projets de communiqués de presse, etc.) et en assurant le suivi de la couverture médiatique. Web • Mettre à jour et assurer la maintenance des pages web CM en respectant les règles et les meilleures pratiques de l'entreprise en matière de web, et garantir une visibilité ainsi qu'une découvrabilité optimales des informations. • Rédiger du contenu web original et adapter des textes pour le web, en respectant les meilleures pratiques en matière de SEO et de GEO. Design et multimédia • Concevoir des supports de communication de haute qualité destinés à diverses parties prenantes (par ex. dépliants, brochures, vidéos, infographies). • Proposer de nouvelles approches et de nouveaux outils promotionnels, conformes aux règles et aux outils de l’Organisation, et se tenir au fait des meilleures pratiques et des innovations au sein de l’OCDE ainsi qu’à l’extérieur. Événements • Gérer les besoins en communication liés aux événements (par ex. conférences, ateliers, webinaires), notamment par la création de sites web ou de pages web dédiés, d'identités visuelles conformément aux règles de l'OCDE en matière de marques, de programmes et d'autres activités promotionnelles. Planification stratégique et communication interne • Contribuer au plan de communication annuel de la DAF et veiller à ce que les activités de communication de CM soutiennent la mise en œuvre de ce plan ainsi que les priorités de communication du Directeur de la DAF. • Collaborer avec les autres chargés de communication de la Division et apporter soutien et renfort en cas de besoin. • Assurer la coordination avec l'unité de communication du bureau du Directeur de la DAF et COM pour la planification des activités de communication. • Soutenir le suivi de l'impact et le partage des connaissances au sein de la Division afin d'optimiser la portée des actions et de favoriser l'échange de bonnes pratiques. item.title: Product Manager
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . ITS Vice Presidency Context: The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Department Context: ITS Operations and Country Engagement Department (ITSOE) delivers innovative products and services to frontline staff working on over 6,000 projects throughout every Region and Global Practice. Our teams support and enable Bank priorities, boost operations efficiency and effectiveness, and facilitate Operational knowledge discovery. Our delivery model leverages global expertise, design and architecture, leading technology, and robust processes to deliver business solutions that ensure value for money. Unit Context: The ITS Country Engagement unit (ITSCE) provides digital support for global and country-specific products, aiding thousands of task teams and country management units in better planning, tracking, and managing their operations, thereby improving country engagement. Additionally, ITSCE enables geospatial capabilities through self-service tools and analytics, allowing teams to monitor project preparation and implementation from anywhere. The Geospatial Solutions team is responsible for the delivery, evolution, and adoption of enterprise geospatial products and services that support operational, analytical, and decision-support needs across the World Bank Group. The team develops and manages platforms that integrate geospatial, statistical, and development data to generate location-based insights supporting country programs, project design and implementation, infrastructure planning, climate resilience, disaster risk management, results monitoring, and other operational priorities. The ITSCE unit is seeking a Product Manager who is passionate about geospatial technologies and committed to maximizing business value through technology delivery. The role will lead business engagement and product strategy for the Geospatial Solutions portfolio, working closely with operational stakeholders, Country Management Units, Global Practices, regional teams, and technology partners to identify opportunities, shape demand, and ensure geospatial investments deliver measurable operational impact. The Product Manager will play a key role in connecting development and operational needs with innovative geospatial capabilities while ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and technology strategy. Duties and responsibilities • Leads the product portfolio for Geospatial Solutions, working with agile team and Country Management Units, Global Practices, Regional teams, and operational stakeholders to identify high-value opportunities where geospatial solutions can improve development outcomes, operational efficiency, decision-making, and project delivery. • Deep understanding of business and operational priorities across regions and sectors, and translates these needs into geospatial product strategies, roadmaps, and investment priorities. • Defines and communicates a clear, scalable product vision and roadmap for Geospatial solutions that balances operational demand, delivery capacity, organizational priorities, and long-term sustainability. • Builds strategic relationships across the WBG and with external partner organizations to advance the adoption and impact of geospatial solutions. • Promotes the use of geospatial intelligence and spatial analytics in support of country programs, project implementation, climate resilience, disaster response, infrastructure planning, and monitoring and evaluation activities. • Provides leadership across agile teams, ensuring alignment, coordination, and execution so that development cycles translate into timely, high-quality product releases and operational value. • Facilitates continuous stakeholder engagement and feedback, identifies emerging opportunities, and evolves the product roadmap to maximize adoption and business impact across operational teams. • Designs governance structures and operating models for geospatial products, ensuring compliance with WBG policies, technology standards, and data management requirements while maintaining agility and innovation. • Oversees vendor and partner relationships, ensuring timely access to specialized geospatial expertise, technical capabilities, and delivery support. • Evaluates and recommends strategic investments that accelerate product development, improve scalability, enable replication across regions and business units, and effectively manage technical debt. • Monitors product-level financials and investment performance, ensuring resources are utilized effectively and aligned with business value and operational outcomes. • Leads complex, cross-functional initiatives involving software engineers, data scientists, GIS specialists, solution architects, business stakeholders, and operational teams to deliver impactful geospatial capabilities. • Identifies systemic challenges and cross-cutting opportunities across sectors and regions, applying structured analysis and strategic thinking to accelerate the adoption of geospatial solutions throughout the World Bank Group. • Represents the Geospatial Solutions portfolio in strategic discussions and governance forums, advocating for investments and priorities that support operational effectiveness and development impact.

item.title: Underwriter
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) is a member of the World Bank Group with a mission to promote foreign direct investment into developing countries to help end extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet. MIGA houses the World Bank Group (WBG) guarantee platform which brings together products and experts from the World Bank, International Finance Corporation (IFC), and MIGA for simplicity, efficiency, and speed. MIGA serves as a one-stop shop for all WBG guarantee business, providing the best guarantee solutions for clients to meet project needs and development priorities. The platform provides three types of coverages: credit guarantees for loans to the public or private sector; trade finance guarantees for trade finance projects involving public entities; and political risk insurance against non-commercial risks for private sector projects or public-private partnerships. For more information, visit www.miga.org . In February 2024, the World Bank Group announced a major upgrade to its guarantees business, by establishing as of July 1 2024, the Guarantee Platform (Platform) housed at MIGA. The Platform will deliver improved guarantee access through a unified team of guarantee specialists as well as innovative new guarantee solutions. These new reforms will help position the Platform/MIGA to achieve the goal of tripling annual guarantee issuance to $20 billion by 2030. MIGA’s Operations Department (MIGOP) leads MIGA’s guarantee business development and origination activities, structures transactions, leads projects through the underwriting and approval process, and manages guarantees portfolio. Within MIGOP, the Global Transaction Team (GTT) is a dedicated team of Analysts, Underwriters, and Senior Underwriters with a focus on underwriting MIGA’s guarantee transactions. MIGOP is seeking a highly experienced, motivated, and proactive Underwriter with strong project finance, public sector finance, political risk insurance, trade finance and/or structured finance underwriting skills, as well as client and new business origination skills, preferably gained in the energy and general infrastructure or financial sectors. While reporting to the Manager for GTT, the day to day activities of the Underwriter will focus mainly on leading transaction teams (comprised of individuals from across the Agency/Platform) and underwriting guarantee transactions as the transaction lead. Depending on experience, the activities may also include supporting business origination and transaction structuring activities. Through this role, the underwriter will develop a broad knowledge of the Platform’s guarantee activities by working on transactions across the Platform’s full product line and across regions and sectors (energy and extractives industries, infrastructure, financial institutions, capital markets, manufacturing, agriculture, services, etc.). Note that this is initially a Washington, DC-based position, however given the regionalization agenda, there is a strong possibility of this position being selected for decentralization. If shortlisted, this will be discussed with you at interview. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES • Lead a multi-disciplinary transaction team (sector, legal, environment and social, climate finance, reinsurance, gender, integrity, risk, development impact, etc.) through the transaction underwriting and approval process, which includes the organization and coordination of due diligence meetings and missions. • Conduct sector and project risk assessments, including contractual risk allocation and the technical and commercial viability of the investment project • Prepare and use complex financial models to, amongst others, analyze the financial viability of the investment project or support credit analysis for credit enhancement transactions • Work together with the risk management officers to analyze country/sub-sovereign project risks and mitigants and with the credit risk officers to support the analysis of state-owned enterprises (credit profile, institutional capacity, legal status and relationship with the government) • Collaborate with risk management officers and the transaction team to conduct development impact analyses of investment projects, including assessing the contribution to the host country's development, the broader impact on the industry and the private sector, and the benefits delivered to both direct and indirect stakeholders • Develop, together with the transaction team, recommendations for the contract of guarantee terms and conditions, including recommendations on appropriate guarantee structures and risk mitigants • Lead the negotiation of new contracts of guarantee with prospective guarantee holders and/or their advisors, in close coordination with the relevant Team Lead/Sector Manager and MIGA’s Legal Department • Engage closely with MIGA’s clients, conduct in-country and virtual due diligence meetings with host country government officials, and collaborate with partners (e.g., World Bank, IFC, and other development finance partners) • Prepare high quality guarantee proposal documents and present them for consideration to MIGA’s Senior Management and Board of Executive Directors • In close coordination with MIGA Senior/Sector Underwriters, Sector Managers, and Regional Heads, support MIGA’s new business origination and client management efforts aimed at generating a robust pipeline of business • As required, create and deliver new business origination-focused presentations to sponsors, government officials, state-owned enterprises, financial institutions, specialist industry groups, and forums
