item.title: E T Consultant, Investment Analyst, Financial Institutions Group, Peru
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org. The FIG’s Latin America and the Caribbean team (FIG LAC) is based across the LAC region with main hubs and locations in Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, and Sao Paulo. The team members work on both new business development and processing, and portfolio management across the region. FIG is seeking to hire an ET Consultant to be based in Lima, Peru. The ET Consultant will be integrated into the team that develops new business, completes transactions, and supervises a portfolio of loans, quasi-equity and equity investments in FIG’s LAC region. The candidate is required to know and effectively use fundamental business concepts and practices and to provide analytical, research and other professional support to professional level Investment Officers. The work program is varied and may be somewhat complex requiring evaluation, original thinking, and various written outputs. Duties and Accountabilities • Create financial analysis models. • Support structuring of new investments. • Analyze historical and projected financial statements and prepare periodic portfolio reports. • Conduct industry and market research and assist in IFC’s business development efforts. • Monitor operational and financial performance of client companies to evaluate risk and recommend active portfolio management actions. • Prepare documentation for IFC internal processes and monitor compliance with IFC financial, environmental and legal requirements. • Establish and maintain quality client relationships to ensure responsive client service and to enhance new business opportunities. • Participate in investments negotiations. • Liaise with colleagues across departments and the region and at the head office in Washington DC. • Participate in the monitoring of investments in portfolio companies.

item.title: ETC - Disaster Risk Finance /Insurance and Modeling Expert
item.description: Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty on a livable planet, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . Prosperity Vice Presidency The WBG Prosperity Vice Presidency is responsible for getting the right public and private sector solutions to our operational teams and to our clients, and to produce scalable impact. It l eads the WBG’s key global engagements in support of: Growth and jobs (including supporting teams across the WBG on the jobs agenda); debt sustainability and debt management; improved domestic resource mobilization and expenditure efficiency; a resilient and inclusive financial sector; business-enabling policies and regulations; trade policy and facilitation; and transparent, effective, and accountable government institutions world-wide. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission. Financial Services Sector (FSS) I Department The FSS Global Department is comprised of two directorates: FSS I covers financial resilience and integrity, financial inclusion, capital market development and disaster risk finance, while FSS II covers SME finance, Banking, Housing, Leasing and Insurance, as well as Sustainable Finance. Disaster Risk Finance Unit The Disaster Risk Finance (DRF) team in FSS1 helps client governments strengthen financial resilience to disaster shocks. Through the Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program (DRFIP), the team delivers technical assistance, analytical work, and advisory support, drawing on the World Bank’s crisis preparedness and response toolkit and other financial instruments. It works closely with regional and country teams, government counterparts, private sector, development partners to design and implement solutions tailored to each country’s risk profile and institutional context. The DRF team also contributes to global efforts to close insurance protection gaps, including through engagement with the G7, G20, the International Association of Insurance Supervisors, and the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), among others. Against this background, the DRF team seeks an Extended Term Consultant (ETC) to provide senior-level technical advice and engagement support for the Unit’s work program on DRFI, insurance market development, and risk modeling. The position is based in London, United Kingdom, and requires frequent travel. Duties and Responsibilities The ETC will be responsible for the following: • Lead the delivery of disaster risk finance instruments and mechanisms in countries, including sovereign risk transfer products such as parametric insurance, catastrophe bonds, and risk pooling arrangements, as well as contingent financing facilities, disaster reserve funds, and risk-based public financial management frameworks. • Provide ad hoc actuarial and quantitative analysis to support client engagement, policy dialogue, and internal decision-making, including identifying options to strengthen financial protection across risk layers undertaking value for money analysis. • Review and quality-assure technical outputs prepared by others, including diagnostic reports, strategy documents, financial models, and presentations. • Curate and share knowledge on insurance market development, including key bottlenecks, global trends, insurance technology, the integration of insurance into climate risk management, relevant case studies, and financial innovations for client countries. This may include co-authoring policy and research notes, preparing internal guidance, developing policy and industry toolkits, and organizing seminars and workshops. • Collaborate with internal stakeholders such as IFC, MIGA, Treasury, and external stakeholders, including the Insurance Development Forum (IDF). • Represent the CDRFI team in stakeholder consultations, interagency coordination forums, workshops, and donor dialogues, as needed. • Perform other duties and tasks assigned by the Unit Manager. The initial appointment will be for one year, with possible renewal for up to two additional years, subject to business needs, funding availability, and satisfactory performance. Under World Bank Group policy, Extended Term appointments are limited to a lifetime maximum of three years.

Duties Responsibilities: The ETC will be responsible for the following: • Lead or contribute to work on insurance regulatory, supervisory, and market practices, including supporting or leading country-level engagements through relevant financing operations and advisory and knowledge activities; • Develop, curate, and share knowledge on insurance market development, including key bottlenecks, emerging global trends, the integration of insurance into climate risk management, insurance technology, relevant case studies, and financial innovations for client countries. The initial appointment will be for one year, with the possibility of renewal for up to an additional two years, subject to business needs, funding availability, and satisfactory performance. item.title: Analyste de la sécurité et des réseaux électriques
item.description: {"id":"744000141302924","name":"Analyste de la sécurité et des réseaux électriques","uuid":"6ce1fc74-96e7-44d6-ac3d-2569690427f7","jobId":"95140137-15e3-49d4-a9e8-415e9e9c7dcf","jobAdId":"d8cc7ab4-681b-4b13-a3d1-829f05d0f2b9","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3341X","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000727","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"5a9445ef-058b-4346-8dca-ef49c8638ded","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL6","valueLabel":"PAL6"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-03T15:59:10.562Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141302924-analyste-de-la-securite-et-des-reseaux-electriques","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141302924-analyste-de-la-securite-et-des-reseaux-electriques?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/6ce1fc74-96e7-44d6-ac3d-2569690427f7?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. L’ Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) est une organisation intergouvernementale qui œuvre en faveur de la sécurité des approvisionnements énergétiques, de la croissance économique et de la durabilité environnementale en promouvant la coopération dans le domaine des politiques énergétiques. L’AIE fonctionne en tant qu’organe autonome au sein de l’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques. L’AIE recherche des analystes de la sécurité et des réseaux électriques pour contribuer à ses travaux d’analyse des réseaux et de l’électrification menés au sein de sa Division des systèmes et marchés de l’électricité (ESM). Les personnes retenues prendront part aux travaux de la Division sur la sécurité de l’approvisionnement en électricité et, en particulier, la modernisation des réseaux de transport et de distribution. Il s’agira d’analyser et de modéliser les systèmes électriques sous l’angle physique et techno-économique, et d’élaborer des projets axés sur les réseaux. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Modélisation, analyse et rédaction Piloter les travaux techniques, d’analyse et de modélisation de la Division consacrés aux systèmes électriques, à la modernisation des réseaux (transport et distribution) et à la sécurité de l’approvisionnement en électricité. Conduire des travaux d’analyse portant sur les moyens d’intégrer au système les nouvelles sources de production d’électricité et les nouvelles formes de demande, en mettant l’accent sur la sécurité d’exploitation, la fiabilité et la résilience. Analyser les évolutions de la gestion de la congestion, des processus de raccordement au réseau et de la planification stratégique des réseaux sur les principaux marchés de l’électricité. Suivre les innovations et les pratiques opérationnelles visant à permettre une utilisation plus efficiente des réseaux, notamment les technologies d’amélioration des réseaux, les solutions numériques et les cadres de réglementation. Contribuer à l’exécution du programme de l’AIE relatif à la sécurité de l’approvisionnement en électricité, et prendre part à la rédaction de contenus relatifs au réseau pour le rapport de l’AIE sur l’électricité et d’autres publications pertinentes de la Division des systèmes et marchés de l’électricité. Collaboration et relations avec l’extérieur Échanger avec les principales parties prenantes du secteur ; prêter son concours, en tant que de besoin, aux préparatifs des réunions des comités permanents, des groupes de travail et, si nécessaire, d’autres groupes de l’AIE ; participer aux réunions pertinentes d’autres organisations internationales ; concourir à l’établissement des rapports, analyses et éléments d’information destinés à ces réunions. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil idéal Formation Diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur ou doctorat en génie électrique, génie énergétique, génie des systèmes énergétiques, économie de l’énergie, physique ou dans une discipline connexe. Expérience professionnelle Au moins cinq à sept ans d’expérience directement acquise sur les systèmes électriques dans une entreprise du secteur de l’électricité, une société de conseil économique, une entreprise axée sur les technologies de réseau ou une autorité de réglementation de l’électricité, en travaillant sur les réseaux de transport ou de distribution, l’exploitation des systèmes, la gestion de l’énergie ou un domaine connexe. Solide connaissance technique des systèmes électriques et compréhension approfondie des concepts liés à la sécurité de l’approvisionnement en électricité, des fondamentaux du marché de l’électricité et de l’interaction entre l’exploitation du système et les incitations du marché. Solide connaissance des réseaux de distribution de moyenne et de basse tension, avec une bonne compréhension des cadres régissant les processus de raccordement et l’intégration des ressources énergétiques décentralisées. Une expérience de la planification du réseau et des pratiques opérationnelles visant à améliorer l’efficience et l’utilisation des infrastructures existantes est souhaitable. Une expérience de la modélisation des systèmes électriques, notamment la modélisation des réseaux en régime stationnaire, en régime dynamique ou en stabilité transitoire, ou de l’étude de la planification ou de l’extension du réseau constituerait un avantage. Capacités d’analyse avérées et excellente compétence rédactionnelle, confirmées par les produits de travaux antérieurs (rapports analytiques, analyses quantitatives, modèles opératoires et/ou textes publiés). Outils Excellente maîtrise des applications Microsoft Office, en particulier d’Excel. Une expérience de SQL ou Power Query constituerait un atout. Solide connaissance de langages de programmation pertinents (Python par exemple). Une expérience de logiciels de modélisation de réseau pertinents (PowerFactory, PSS, PSCAD, par exemple) constituerait un avantage. Langues Excellente maîtrise de l’anglais à l’écrit et à l’oral, avec des compétences rédactionnelles et éditoriales. La connaissance d’une ou de plusieurs autres langues constituerait un atout. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Informations supplémentaires","text":" Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 2) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 2) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 2) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2). Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de maîtrise 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE . Durée du contrat Durée déterminée de deux ans, avec possibilité de renouvellement. Veuillez noter que, conformément aux Statut et Règlement applicables aux agents de l’Organisation, l’âge de départ obligatoire à la retraite est fixé à 67 ans. Ce qu’offre l’OCDE Le salaire mensuel minimum s’élève à 8 098.36 EUR, plus allocations/indemnités en fonction de la situation personnelle, la rémunération globale étant exonérée d’impôt sur le revenu en France. Cliquez ici pour consulter les Statut, règlement et instructions applicables aux agents de l’OCDE. Veuillez noter que toute personne nommée agent·e à compter du 1er juillet 2025 sera engagée conformément aux nouvelles modalités contractuelles de l’OCDE . Cliquez ici pour en savoir plus sur ce que propose l’OCDE et sur son environnement de travail exceptionnel. Cliquez ici pour feuilleter en ligne notre Guide de gestion du personnel afin d’en savoir plus sur tous les aspects touchant aux ressources humaines de l’Organisation, à notre environnement de travail et aux nombreuses autres mesures destinées à faciliter le quotidien des agents. Veuillez noter que la personne retenue pourra être engagée à un grade inférieur, en fonction de ses qualifications et de son expérience professionnelle. La présente offre d’emploi servira à la constitution d’un vivier de candidat·es jugé·es aptes à exercer des fonctions compar

item.description: {"id":"744000141302735","name":"Electricity Grids and Security Analyst","uuid":"ead9fc3e-8e6a-4885-a190-bce906819480","jobId":"95140137-15e3-49d4-a9e8-415e9e9c7dcf","jobAdId":"fdf70a81-bda1-4dc9-a906-c1d720873d47","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3341X","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000727","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"5a9445ef-058b-4346-8dca-ef49c8638ded","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL6","valueLabel":"PAL6"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-03T16:01:27.490Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141302735-electricity-grids-and-security-analyst","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141302735-electricity-grids-and-security-analyst?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/ead9fc3e-8e6a-4885-a190-bce906819480?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The International Energy Agency (IEA) is an intergovernmental organisation committed to advancing security of energy supply, economic growth and environmental sustainability through energy policy co-operation. The IEA operates as an autonomous body within the framework of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). The IEA seeks to recruit Electricity Grids and Security Analysts to contribute to its analytical work on grids and electrification in the Electricity Systems and Markets Division (ESM). The Electricity Gris and Security Analysts will support the Division’s work on electricity security, with a particular focus on transmission and distribution system modernisation. This includes to analyse and model power systems from physical and technoeconomic perspectives, and to draft grid-focused projects. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Modelling, analysis and drafting Lead the Division’s technical, analytical and modelling work on power systems, grid modernisation (transmission and distribution), and electricity security. Lead analytical work on the system integration of emerging sources of electricity demand and generation, with a focus on operational security, reliability and resilience. Analyse developments in congestion management, grid connection processes, and strategic grid planning across key power markets. Monitor innovations and operational practices aimed at enabling more efficient use of grids, including Grid Ehancing Technologies (GETs), digital solutions, and regulatory frameworks. Contribute to the delivery of the IEA’s Electricity Security programme and to drafting grid-related content for the IEA’s Electricity report and other relevant ESM publications. Collaboration and outreach Engage with key industry stakeholders; support preparations as needed for meetings of IEA standing committees, working parties and other groups as required; participate in relevant meetings of other international organisations; provide support for the development of reports, analyses and information items for these meetings. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background Advanced university degree or PhD in Electrical / Power / Energy Systems Engineering, Energy Economics, Physics or a related discipline. Professional Background At least five years to seven years of direct power systems work experience in the electricity industry, economic consulting, grid technology companies, or at an electric regulatory agency working on transmission or distribution networks, system operation, energy management and related fields. Strong technical background in power systems and in-depth understanding of electricity security concepts, power market fundamentals, and the interaction between system operations and market incentives. Solid knowledge of medium- and low-voltage distribution grids, with an understanding of the frameworks governing connection processes and the integration of distributed energy resources. Experience with network planning and operational practices aimed at enhancing the efficiency and utilisation of existing infrastructure is desirable. Experience with power system modelling, such as steady‑state network modelling, dynamic and transient stability modelling, or grid planning and expansion studies, would be an advantage. Proven analytical abilities and excellent writing skills as demonstrated in past work products (analytical reports, quantitative analysis, operative models, and/or published papers). Tools Excellent command of Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel. Experience with SQL or Power Query is an asset. Solid knowledge of relevant coding languages (e.g. Python). Experience with relevant grid modelling software (e.g. PowerFactory, PSS, PSCAD) would be an advantage. Languages Excellent written and oral command of English, including drafting and proofreading. Knowledge of one or more other working languages would be an asset. item.description: {"id":"744000141418699","name":"Gestionnaire de projet et Coordinateur/trice RH","uuid":"85d50aa7-cd2e-41a2-9c3b-673d8850634d","jobId":"ccf1c75d-7d0c-468f-acd4-f09ab436a463","jobAdId":"4f3f705c-978a-4b09-984c-bd848032377b","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3339V","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000727","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"7038891","valueLabel":"Corporate Functions"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"CF3","valueLabel":"CF3"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-04T06:49:42.299Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141418699-gestionnaire-de-projet-et-coordinateur-trice-rh","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141418699-gestionnaire-de-projet-et-coordinateur-trice-rh?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/85d50aa7-cd2e-41a2-9c3b-673d8850634d?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. L’ Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) est une organisation intergouvernementale de 32 pays Membres qui œuvre en faveur de la sécurité des approvisionnements énergétiques, de la croissance économique et de la durabilité environnementale en promouvant la coopération dans le domaine des politiques énergétiques. L’AIE fonctionne en tant qu’organe autonome au sein de l’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques (OCDE). L’OCDE et l’AIE recherchent l’une et l’autre des occasions de collaborer avec un nombre croissant de non-Membres qui jouent un rôle de plus en plus important dans l’économie mondiale. L’AIE entend favoriser la contribution du secteur de l’énergie au développement économique et à la durabilité environnementale. L’AIE recherche un(e) gestionnaire de projet et coordinateur/trice des ressources humaines pour coordonner au niveau d’une équipe les opérations liées aux RH et à l’administration du personnel et pour soutenir la stratégie de développement des talents, les projets RH et les initiatives d’achat connexes de l’Agence. La personne retenue relèvera de la Conseillère principale chargée des ressources humaines de l’AIE et travaillera en étroite collaboration avec la personne responsable des ressources humaines et l’équipe chargée des ressources humaines à l’AIE, l’Unité des finances, les responsables et les autres membres du personnel de l’AIE, ainsi qu’avec les équipes de gestion des ressources humaines de l’OCDE, les prestataires de formation externes et les équipes chargées des achats à l’OCDE. Elle supervisera le déroulement rapide et efficient des opérations courantes des équipes chargées des RH à l’AIE en matière de RH et d’administration du personnel. Elle élaborera et mettra en œuvre les projets et initiatives de l’AIE en faveur du développement des talents et de la gestion du changement à l’intention du personnel de l’AIE. Elle jouera un rôle consultatif dans des domaines clés. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Gestion de projet - Initiatives en faveur de la gestion des talents et de l’efficience organisationnelle Concevoir, mettre en œuvre et suivre les projets de l’AIE tels que les programmes d’apprentissage et de gestion du changement, en veillant à ce qu'ils correspondent aux priorités de l’Organisation et en produisant des résultats mesurables. Gérer en autonomie la planification des projets et la coordination des initiatives de formation et d’accompagnement, en veillant à leur bonne exécution et à la mobilisation de différentes parties prenantes à l’échelle de l’Agence. Contribuer à la mise en œuvre et à l’amélioration continue par l’AIE des lignes directrices et outils RH, en étroite coordination avec la Conseillère principale chargée des ressources humaines et les équipes RH concernées. Superviser la conception et le déploiement de campagnes axées sur l’attraction des talents et le recrutement générique à l’AIE, en tant que de besoin, en veillant au respect des délais et des exigences et à la réalisation des résultats escomptés, en étroite coordination avec les chargé(e)s des ressources humaines. Coordonner les initiatives en faveur des talents au sein de l’équipe OMA/HR, en favorisant et en pilotant des projets visant à améliorer l’efficience de la gestion des talents à l’échelle de l’Agence, en collaboration avec la Conseillère principale chargée des ressources humaines. Contribuer à la mise en œuvre des initiatives de réforme RH, en veillant à leur alignement sur les objectifs de l’Organisation, en tant que de besoin. Coordination RH et services consultatifs Diriger et coordonner les actions relatives au personnel de l’AIE (contrats, mobilité du personnel, évolution de carrière, modalités de télétravail, absences, suivi des rapports sur la période probatoire, etc.) au sein de l’équipe OMA/HR, en veillant à leur rapidité d’exécution, à leur qualité et au respect des règles et en fournissant des orientations aux membres de l’équipe en tant que de besoin. Analyser et piloter les initiatives d’amélioration des processus RH, en repensant les flux de travail pour gagner en efficience, rationaliser les opérations et accélérer la prestation de services dans le domaine des activités d’administration du personnel. Suivre et accompagner la mise en œuvre des politiques, réformes, lignes directrices et bonnes pratiques de l’Organisation en matière de ressources humaines, en veillant à leur adoption effective et à leur harmonisation au sein de l’Agence, via un processus régulier de renforcement des capacités, en fonction des besoins. Veiller au renforcement des capacités et communiquer régulièrement aux différentes parties prenantes des informations sur les projets de réforme et d’efficience RH, en tant que de besoin. Jouer un rôle consultatif de premier plan auprès du personnel et des clients internes eu égard aux politiques, procédures opérationnelles et meilleures pratiques RH, grâce à une communication et des orientations claires. Gérer la coordination des ressources humaines pour les programmes des Jeunes Associés (YAP) et Jeunes Experts Associés (JEA) en tant que gestionnaire de projet dédié(e), notamment l’examen préalable des candidatures, à l’appui des processus d’évaluation (tests et examen). Superviser la coordination des opérations courantes en matière de RH, y compris par le biais de comptes rendus et d’échanges hebdomadaires avec les équipes de gestion des ressources humaines de l’OCDE. Développer et appliquer une connaissance approfondie des cadres de gestion des ressources humaines de l’OCDE, en veillant à ce que l’ensemble des activités, projets et processus soient conformes aux politiques et pratiques de l’OCDE. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil idéal Formation Diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur, assorti d’une formation en gestion des ressources humaines ou d’une expérience équivalente acquise dans le cadre de fonctions similaires. Expérience professionnelle Au moins 5 ans d’expérience professionnelle acquise dans le cadre de fonctions similaires de gestion des ressources humaines. Expérience de la conception, de la mise en œuvre et du suivi de programmes d’apprentissage et de gestion du changement, et de la coordination des achats avec divers prestataires. Expérience avérée de la conception et du déploiement de mesures au service de l’efficience des opérations RH, d’une part, et de l’orientation et de la coordination des efforts d’une équipe pour veiller au respect des KPI, d’autre part. Excellent sens de la planification et de l’organisation. Aptitudes avérées à anticiper et à faire face à une multiplicité de demandes RH ainsi qu’à des délais stricts, à communiquer clairement et à travailler efficacement dans un environnement multiculturel. Une bonne connaissance des Statut, règlement et instructions applicables aux agents de l’Organisation et de leurs modalités de mise en œuvre, ainsi que du Règlement financier de l’OCDE et de ses Règles d’application, constituerait un avantage. Une expérience acquise dans un environnement international constituerait un avantage. Outils Très bonne connaissance des applications de gestion des ressources telles que SAP, OBMR, Business Objects (BO), SmartRecruiters, PowerBI ou Concur, ou aptitude à maîtriser très rapidement

item.title: Director General, WBG Independent Accountability Mechanism
item.description: Identifying and addressing environmental and social (E S) risks is critical to the World Bank Group (WBG)’s mission of ending poverty and promoting shared prosperity on a livable planet. To ensure that E S issues are properly identified and addressed, the WBG has put in place policies and procedures that guide WBG staff when they are supporting the design, implementation, and supervision of WBG-financed operations. The WBG has made significant efforts to leverage its private and public sector arms to provide better results and integrated solutions for its clients. To this end, a new integrated WBG E S structure has been established to better support public- and private-sector clients in achieving their sustainable development objectives and to establish a more robust system for proactive risk management. This new structure aims to: (i) ensure that attention to E S matters remains constant during the project life cycle; (ii) facilitate escalation of issues for rapid response; and (iii) strengthen technical oversight to ensure E S risks are flagged, monitored, and adequately addressed. Ultimately, the new E S structure aims to further strengthen development outcomes through better implementation of WBG E S policies in WBG-financed operations. To ensure that the WBG accountability framework remains effective and fit for purpose, on June 8, 2026, the Boards of Executive Directors of IBRD/IDA, IFC, and MIGA (“the WBG Boards”) established a new, single WBG Independent Accountability Mechanism (WBG IAM). This new WBG IAM builds on decades of operational experience, institutional knowledge, and best practices of the IFC/MIGA Compliance Advisor Ombudsman (“CAO”), the WB Inspection Panel (“IPN”), and the WB Dispute Resolution Service (“DRS”). Its primary role remains to provide an independent and accessible forum for people who believe that they have been, or are likely to be, adversely affected by a WBG-financed operation to file a complaint and seek recourse, improve accountability and learning, facilitate dispute resolution, ensure compliance with the E S policies of the WBG, enhance E S sustainability and reduce the risk of harm to people and environment. The WBG embraces the vital role that a robust independent accountability mechanism plays in its broader role as a development institution. To ensure that E S issues are properly addressed, the WBG is committed to reinforcing the WBG IAM as a credible, effective, and responsive mechanism to help deliver environmentally and socially sound operations and enhance the WBG’s contribution to sustainable development. The WBG IAM serves as a forum for addressing the concerns of project-affected people in a manner that is independent, fair, and constructive. For this reason, the IAM is headed by a Director General (DG) reporting directly to the WBG Boards, under the oversight of CODE, and is independent from WBG operational management. About the World Bank Group Independent Accountability Mechanism To discharge its mandate, the WBG IAM has three functions: Dispute Resolution (DR) . Through Dispute Resolution, the mechanism works with affected communities and WBG clients to resolve grievances using a voluntary, flexible, neutral, and collaborative problem-solving approach, including mediation, negotiation, and facilitated dialogue. Compliance. Through its Compliance function, the mechanism serves as an independent, factfinding investigative body on behalf of the WBG Boards. In the case of public sector operations, the mechanism assesses the Bank’s alleged failure to follow its operational policies and procedures with respect to the design, appraisal, and/or implementation/supervision of a project financed by the Bank. For complaints on private sector operations, the mechanism carries out reviews of IFC/MIGA compliance with their E S obligations set out in the Sustainability Framework , assesses related harm, and recommends remedial actions to address non-compliance and harm where appropriate. The compliance function is not a judicial, quasi-judicial, or legal enforcement mechanism, nor is it designed as a substitute for national courts or regulatory processes. Advisory. The IAM’s advisory function provides independent and ad hoc advice to the WBG Boards and Management on systemic issues identified from case data with the view of improving WBG performance on E S sustainability and reducing the risk of harm to people and the environment. Duties and Responsibilities The WBG IAM DG will be appointed by and will report to the WBG Boards under the oversight of the Committee on Development Effectiveness (CODE). The DG is directly accountable to the Boards and is not part of, and does not report to, Management. The DG’s key duties and responsibilities include: • Supporting the development and implementation of the new WBG IAM policy; facilitating the transition process from the current accountability system to the new WBG IAM; and leading the change management required to integrate WBG IAM operations, while safeguarding the IAM’s independence and credibility. • Ensuring the effective functioning of the IAM’s three arms—Dispute Resolution, Compliance, and Advisory—by overseeing cases, meeting timelines, maintaining process integrity and quality control, establishing internal procedures and guidelines with DR, Compliance, and Advisory staff, and supervising the receipt, acknowledgment, eligibility assessment, and further processing of complaints. • Directing complex, multi-disciplinary investigations and ensuring impartial and thorough factfinding. • Managing the IAM’s day-to-day operations, including planning, directing, and organizing its work program, budget, and staff performance, while ensuring budget resources are managed in line with relevant WBG rules, policies, and internal controls. • Presenting IAM budget requests to the Boards annually and ensuring adherence to budgetary levels established by the WBG Boards. • Monitoring and reporting on key performance indicators to assess the IAM’s continued effectiveness, tracking progress against institutional objectives, and supporting continuous improvement. • Communicating with complainants and affected parties while managing retaliation risks and safeguarding confidential business information; maintaining appropriate communication with relevant WBG departments; and fostering strong relationships with key stakeholders, including requesters, civil society organizations, academia, and other relevant parties. • Providing strategic leadership to the IAM team, overseeing delivery of the IAM’s objectives, goals, guidelines, and work programs, and managing staff while fostering a culture of integrity and inclusion, supporting professional development, and ensuring compliance with applicable administrative, staff rules and workplace standards. • Hiring staff and consultants/independent contractors as needed, in line with Bank policies, procedures, and with due attention to budget considerations; resolving issues arising from coordination across IAM functions; and managing staff, including approving work programs and administrative matters such as contracts, leave, mission travel, and expenses. Building and maintaining as needed a roster of independent experts (e.g., in areas such as mediation, dispute resolution, compliance, auditing, resettlement, indigenous peoples, E S safeguard policies, among others). • Ensuring the integrity, quality, coherence, and accuracy of IAM reports, findings, recommendations, and other products, in line with applicable Bank policies and procedures. • Representing the IAM in public and private fora, overseeing stakeholder outreach and guidance, and ensuring that the IAM’s website, public registry, archive system, and social media provide current, relevant, and accurate information on its work and activities. • Meeting regularly with the relevant Board Committee Chairs to keep the Committees and the Boards informed of the IAM’s activities, preparing reports for the Boards as needed, and performing other IAM-related functions as assigned by the WBG Boards. • Ensuring and safeguarding independence from all stakeholders possibly linked to a case and maintaining its reporting line to the Boards. • During the transition period the DG will report periodically to the Board through CODE and participate in the development of the new IAM policy, taking into consideration the Board’s decision on the seven policy principles and building on the relevant provisions of the current IAM policies, and lead in its implementation. The DG will also lead in developing the operating procedures for the new IAM, and undertake workforce planning, adjustment of processes and systems while ensuring continuity, credibility, and effectiveness during the transition. • The DG will coordinate with CAO, DRS, and IPN to develop transitional arrangements, including with regard to existing cases, and manage the closure of the current mechanisms while launching the new, integrated WBG IAM. The incumbent for this position will be a full-time staff of the WBG at the level of Vice President, with this level of seniority reflecting the institutional importance of the role. S/he is subject to the confidentiality provisions set forth in WBG policies on access to information and will be subject to the Group Staff Rules and Staff Code of Conduct. The appointment is for a period of five (5) years, non-renewable and s/he will not be employed by the WBG following the end of their term. Only the WBG Boards may terminate the employment of the DG for cause.

item.title: Associate Senior Service Management Officer (Agentic AI & Hyperautomation Portfolio Lead)
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . VPU Context: The World Bank Group (WBG) is accelerating its use of artificial intelligence and automation to enhance operational efficiency, knowledge management, and development impact. As part of this effort, the Information Technology Solutions (ITS) vice presidency—and specifically the ITSSG team—is expanding its capacity in Hyperautomation. This involves integrating advanced AI with core business processes to create a seamless, intelligent automation fabric. A key component of this strategy is the development of agentic AI systems: autonomous, multi-step AI workflows capable of reasoning, tool use, and decision-making. This Terms of Reference outlines the scope of work for a Lead Agentic AI Hyperautomation Strategist at the GG staff level, based in Washington DC, USA to lead the design, strategy, and implementation of these transformative solutions. Objective The Agentic AI Hyperautomation Portfolio Lead will serve as a strategic leader within ITSSG, helping to advance the adoption of Agentic AI, intelligent automation, and AI orchestration capabilities across ITS. Working closely with business, product, architecture, engineering, and platform teams, the role will identify opportunities to drive operational efficiency, improve service delivery, and accelerate digital transformation through AI-powered automation. The successful candidate will influence strategic direction, help shape technology and investment decisions, foster enterprise adoption, and provide leadership across a portfolio of AI and automation initiatives. The role requires a combination of technology expertise, strategic thinking, stakeholder engagement, and the ability to translate emerging capabilities into measurable business outcomes. Scope of Work The staff will be responsible for the following: 1. Strategic Leadership Portfolio Management • Serve as a strategic advisor on Agentic AI, AI orchestration, and Hyperautomation opportunities across ITS. • Help shape priorities, roadmaps, and investment decisions relating to intelligent automation and AI-enabled transformation. • Identify, assess, and prioritize opportunities where Agentic AI and Hyperautomation can deliver measurable operational and business value. • Develop business cases, value realization frameworks, and recommendations to support decision-making and investment planning. • Monitor market developments, emerging technologies, and industry trends, providing guidance on their potential application within WBG. 2. AI Orchestration Hyperautomation Enablement • Promote a cohesive approach to Agentic AI and Hyperautomation across platforms, products, and business domains. • Partner with architecture, engineering, service management, and platform teams to develop scalable patterns and reusable capabilities. • Support the evolution of enterprise AI orchestration capabilities that enable complex workflows spanning multiple systems and technologies. • Influence the design and adoption of solutions that combine AI, workflow automation, and enterprise platforms to improve business outcomes. • Encourage reuse, standardization, and alignment across AI and automation initiatives to maximize value and reduce duplication. 3. Governance, Risk Responsible AI • Support the development and adoption of governance frameworks, standards, and controls for Agentic AI and intelligent automation. • Partner with security, risk, legal, compliance, procurement, and architecture stakeholders to ensure solutions align with institutional policies and standards. • Promote responsible AI practices, including transparency, security, auditability, and operational oversight. • Contribute to the development of guardrails and governance mechanisms that enable innovation while appropriately managing risk. • Advocate for scalable approaches to lifecycle management, monitoring, and operational governance of AI-enabled services. 4. Stakeholder Engagement Organizational Influence • Build strong relationships across ITS and business stakeholders to promote the effective adoption of Agentic AI and Hyperautomation capabilities. • Facilitate alignment across product, platform, architecture, and operational teams on strategic priorities and implementation approaches. • Communicate opportunities, risks, recommendations, and outcomes to senior leaders and governance forums. • Act as a champion for AI-enabled transformation, helping stakeholders understand emerging capabilities and their practical application. • Influence decision-making through collaboration, thought leadership, and trusted advisory relationships. 5. Innovation, Platform Vendor Strategy • Lead assessments of emerging Agentic AI, orchestration, and automation technologies and their applicability within the WBG environment. • Provide recommendations on platform capabilities, technology direction, and strategic investments. • Engage with strategic vendors and industry partners to understand product roadmaps, innovation trends, and emerging capabilities. • Identify opportunities to leverage common enterprise platforms and services to accelerate adoption and value realization. • Foster innovation and knowledge sharing through communities of practice and cross-functional collaboration. 6. Delivery Oversight Value Realization • Provide strategic oversight and guidance across a portfolio of AI and automation initiatives. • Establish measures to track adoption, business value, operational improvements, and organizational impact. • Identify and address barriers to adoption, scalability, and value realization. • Support successful implementation by aligning stakeholders, managing dependencies, and promoting sustainable operating models. • Help ensure initiatives deliver measurable improvements in efficiency, effectiveness, employee experience, and service outcomes.

item.title: Solutions Architect
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . VPU Context The mission of the Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) is to leverage information and technology as a force multiplier to accelerate, deepen, and sustain development impact. Their vision is to harness information and technology for a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information on ITS, check this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w . Department Context ITS Operations and Country Engagement Department (ITSOE) delivers innovative products and services to frontline staff working on over 6,000 projects throughout every Region and Global Practice. Our teams support and enable Bank priorities, boost operations efficiency and effectiveness, and facilitate Operational knowledge discovery. Our delivery model leverages global expertise, design and architecture, leading technology, and robust processes to deliver business solutions that ensure value for money. Unit Context The ITS Country Engagement unit (ITSCE) delivers digital solutions that support global and country-specific products, enables systems aligned with the World Bank Group’s Country Engagement Model, and provides geospatial capabilities that enhance project visibility, spatial analysis, and impact tracking. The unit also drives the design and delivery of AI-powered business solutions that strengthen regional operations and country engagement. The ITSCE unit is seeking a Solutions Architect to define and oversee the technical architecture for digital solutions supporting country teams, including the Country Partnership Framework (CPF) and Country Policy and Institutional Assessment (CPIA) platforms. These products are central to country engagement, strategy development, and operational assessment processes, requiring secure, scalable, maintainable, and well-integrated technology solutions. The Solutions Architect will work closely with country teams, Operations Policy and Country Services (OPCS), product owners, IT delivery teams, platform and security specialists, and operational support teams to ensure solutions align with enterprise architecture standards, technology roadmaps, and the World Bank Group’s strategic priorities. The role is responsible for translating business needs into sustainable technical designs, providing architectural leadership throughout the solution lifecycle, and ensuring the successful delivery of high-quality digital products. Specific Responsibilities: • Define solution architecture, integration patterns, and low- and high-level designs for CPF, CPIA, and related ITSCE Country Solutions products, ensuring alignment with business, enterprise, security, and operational requirements. • Partner with product owners, country teams, OPCS, and IT delivery teams to translate business priorities into feasible solution options, implementation guidance, and technical decisions. • Assess trade-offs, dependencies, risks, non-functional requirements, and total cost of ownership to support secure, scalable, and sustainable technology solutions. • Collaborate with platform, security, infrastructure, and operations teams to ensure solutions align with enterprise architecture standards, technology roadmaps, and operational requirements. • Prepare architecture diagrams, technical presentations, decision records, recommendations, and solution walkthroughs to support alignment, governance, and informed decision-making. • Provide technical leadership throughout the solution lifecycle, including design reviews, implementation guidance, code reviews, and mentoring of engineering teams. • Promote reuse, standardization, interoperability, security-by-design, maintainability, and the responsible adoption of emerging technologies, including AI-enabled capabilities. • Support Agile and SAFe delivery practices by participating in planning, design discussions, technical reviews, and continuous improvement activities.

item.title: Operations Analyst, Eastern Europe
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) is a member of the World Bank Group with a mission to promote foreign direct investment into developing countries to help end extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet. MIGA houses the World Bank Group (WBG) guarantee platform which brings together products and experts from the World Bank, International Finance Corporation (IFC), and MIGA for simplicity, efficiency, and speed. MIGA serves as a one-stop shop for all WBG guarantee business, providing the best guarantee solutions for clients to meet project needs and development priorities. The platform provides three types of coverages: credit guarantees for loans to the public or private sector; trade finance guarantees for trade finance projects involving public entities; and political risk insurance against non-commercial risks for private sector projects or public-private partnerships. For more information, visit www.miga.org . MIGA’s Eastern Europe and Central Asia (ECA) Regional Hub is currently recruiting an Operations Analyst to support MIGA activities in ECA including business development, relationship management with key clients and partners, and coordination of relationships with MIGA stakeholders including shareholders, development partner agencies, development finance institutions, and private sector players in Eastern Europe. The position will be based in Vienna, Austria or Paris, France and, supervised by the Eastern Europe Regional Head. Duties and Accountabilities Business development: • Perform independent research on various topics across different sectors and regions, including preparation of briefing notes for senior management; background information and financial analysis of specific companies; trends in foreign direct investment (FDI); identification of business opportunities across sectors and regions • Conduct mapping of potential clients and partners for MIGA, including coordination with country and sector specific business development strategies • Collect data, analyze, and synthesize data from public and WBG sources for business development and project assessment • Research and identify investor/sector conferences relevant for sectors and regions • Prepare reports, presentations, talking points and minutes for the team and other groups in MIGA • Support relationship activities with clients and partners: use the client management system and provide reports as requested; prepare client pitch books and other marketing presentations; support client meetings and necessary follow-ups • Develop and maintain database and tracking systems related to special sector initiatives Execution: • Assist in underwriting political risk insurance (PRI) and credit enhancement guarantees in various sectors and support team members on complex transactions with an emphasis on financial modeling and credit analysis • Prepare sections of relevant reports (sector updates, sub-sector information, strategy documents, briefing notes, underwriting papers, etc.) and contribute to the formulation of conclusions and recommendations • Liaise with counterparties to ascertain data quality in MIGA databases • Coordinate follow- up as required with sponsors, financiers, and public sector counterparties involved in project specification, definition, bidding preparation, negotiation, awarding of contract and project implementation and monitoring • Track status of projects at various stages in MIGA systems and provide regular updates as agreed with country representative or another designated person • Perform other duties as may be assigned by the manager

item.title: Operations Analyst-Climate and Sustainable Finance Analyst
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org. VPU Context: As part of the World Bank Group’s Planet Vertical, the Climate Department supports WBG delivery on climate and development. It helps operational teams integrate mitigation, adaptation, resilience, and climate risk considerations into projects, programs, analytics, and client engagement. The Department works across WBG institutions, Global Practices, regions, and corporate functions to strengthen delivery, credibility, and consistency. Unit Context: The Climate Department’s Sustainable Finance and Transaction Solutions unit (KTCSS) helps the WBG develop scalable solutions that respond to client demand and support credible implementation across IBRD/IDA, IFC, and MIGA. Its work spans sustainable finance solutions for mitigation and adaptation, climate co-benefits measurement, Paris Alignment, climate risk management, GHG accounting, and climate outcomes metrics. KTCSS also develops the methodologies, tools, and systems needed to mainstream these approaches and support consistent, efficient delivery across operations. It supports operational teams, develops practical guidance and knowledge, strengthens data and reporting, and advances product innovation and data- and AI-enabled solutions. The unit is seeking a versatile analyst to provide analytical, operational, and coordination support across this portfolio. The assignment mix will evolve with team priorities. The role is suited to a strong climate generalist with sound core skills, an interest in climate and sustainable finance, good judgment, and a willingness to learn quickly and roll up their sleeves Duties and accountabilities: •Conduct industry, market, project, and institutional research. Analyze economic, financial, technical, and portfolio data to support operational work, business development, and management decisions. Synthesize findings for different audiences. •Support team workstreams and WBG operations on Paris Alignment, climate co-benefits, sustainable finance, adaptation and resilience, climate risk, and related topics, under guidance from senior colleagues. •Support GHG accounting and climate outcomes metrics. Collect, clean, validate, and analyze data; document assumptions and results; and contribute to improving methodologies, tools, and reporting. This may include gross, net, and financed emissions and resilience outcomes. •Prepare briefs, presentations, reports, guidance, checklists, training and knowledge materials, and communications for internal and external audiences. Support editing, quality review, and dissemination. •Support practical tools, dashboards, data systems, workflow improvements, automation, and AI-enabled solutions, including testing, quality control, user support, and maintenance. •Provide project-management and internal delivery support, including work planning, portfolio monitoring, procurement and contract coordination, meetings and events, stakeholder follow-up, and tracking deliverables. •Collaborate across WBG institutions, regions, Global Practices, operational teams, and corporate functions. Take ownership, respond quickly, shift flexibly between workstreams, and undertake additional assignments as priorities evolve.

item.title: Digital & AI Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, www.worldbank.org Unit(s) Context The South Asia Region The South Asia Region comprises six countries (India, Bhutan, , Maldives, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Sri Lanka) that range in size from India (with a population of over 1 billion) to Maldives (with 0.3 million people). The region has experienced a long period of robust economic growth, averaging 6% a year over the past 20 years. This strong growth has translated into reducing extreme poverty and strong improvements in human development. At the same time, the region remains home to one-third of the world’s poorest, and persistent structural challenges threaten to undermine sustained growth, hindering the region’s ability to create jobs and respond to climate shocks. The South Asia Region: https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/sar Digital AI Vice Presidency Digital technologies offer a unique opportunity to transform development through digital solutions. The Digital AI Vice Presidency and its global and regional teams will support client countries in building the foundational and cross-cutting elements of digital transformation through: • Building broadband connectivity infrastructure, last mile access and data platforms (including last mile connectivity and data infrastructure) • Strengthening digital public infrastructure (DPI), including digital ID, data sharing, verifiable credentials and digitalizing government services that improve accountability and transparency • Protecting institutions, businesses, and citizens through cybersecurity and data protection privacy • Developing ICT sectors and supporting digital entrepreneurship, skills, and jobs • Enabling AI-ready economies by supporting governments in building the policy, regulatory, data, and infrastructure foundations needed to harness AI responsibly and at scale • Supporting the Vice presidencies of People, Prosperity, Planet, and Infrastructure in the digitalization efforts of their clients, and in leveraging digital solutions, including building client sectoral digital capacity, defining and implementing sectoral specific AI strategies, and designing AI-powered solutions For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/digital The roles and responsibilities include but are not limited to: The Opportunity The World Bank Group’s (WBG) engagement on digital development is rapidly growing in the South Asia region (SAR) in response to increased client demand for knowledge, technical assistance, and financing. The overall SAR Digital agenda aims to enhance the speed, scale, and impact of the WBG’s support to enable countries to make the most of digital opportunities and address emerging challenges in an effective and agile manner. SAR Digital Unit is looking for a Digital AI Specialist to be based in New Delhi, India. The position will report to the South Asia Regional Practice Manager for Digital AI and work with the Digital AI team in India, as with other team members based globally. The Specialist will bring hands-on expertise in the design, architecture, and deployment of AI systems in the public sector. Beyond policy and regulatory advice, the role requires the ability to guide governments through the full lifecycle of AI adoption - from use-case identification and feasibility assessment, through solution architecture, data readiness, model selection and procurement, to responsible deployment, monitoring, and scaling. A particular focus will be on applying AI to development challenges in sectors such as health, agriculture, education, social protection, and service delivery, and on building the technical capacity of client institutions to sustain these solutions More specifically, the roles and responsibilities are to: The Digital AI Specialist, together with the Digital AI Team in India, and the broader team will be responsible for Supporting client engagements in India and supervising activities in the sector as a technical expert. These include • Support policy dialogue with senior government officials, coordinate across relevant government agencies, development partners and other World Bank Global Departments and verticals. • Contribute to the design, preparation and supervision of World Bank Group financed investment and policy reform programs on digital and AI, with a particular emphasis on (i) strengthening infrastructure for an AI ready economy, including data centres and cloud, by leveraging private sector investments, (ii) Design and implementation of digital public infrastructure systems for citizen centric service delivery Advise clients on strategies, best practices and design of programs to develop the foundations of their digital economies. This may include participating in technical assistance activities and providing just-in-time technical and strategic expertise on the design of the overall policy, that includes designing national AI strategies, AI governance and regulatory frameworks, data governance regimes, and AI ethics and responsible AI policies that are contextually appropriate for developing country contexts. • Liaise and provide guidance to colleagues working in other sectors (including agriculture, health, education, energy, financial services, transport, etc.) on how to leverage digital technologies and AI to improve public service delivery and efficiency in the respective sectors and to stimulate digital innovation, entrepreneurship and investment in those sectors by private sector actors. • Provide technical leadership on the design and deployment of AI solutions in government, including solution architecture, data pipelines and data readiness assessments, choice of models and platforms (including open-source and frontier models), cloud/compute arrangements, integration with digital public infrastructure, and MLOps/deployment practices appropriate for public sector environments. • Advise clients on sectoral AI applications for development — e.g., AI for health diagnostics and supply chains, agricultural advisory services, personalized learning, social protection targeting and G2P delivery — including assessing use-case feasibility, cost, risks, and pathways to scale. • Support clients in operationalizing responsible AI in deployed systems, including bias testing, safety evaluations, human-in-the-loop design, grievance redress, and post-deployment monitoring. • Contribute to building client-side technical capacity for AI adoption, including institutional arrangements (e.g., AI units/centers of excellence), procurement approaches for AI systems, and talent and skills strategies.

item.description: {"id":"744000141742372","name":"Junior Power Sector Analyst","uuid":"fa9ad93f-ffb7-4a9d-b501-af2d11b2eb4b","jobId":"f204b628-f7b3-4abf-af0e-b0b5f4e2ad25","jobAdId":"430beef4-4469-4dd7-a0ff-992f29633839","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3349P","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000727","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"5a9445ef-058b-4346-8dca-ef49c8638ded","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL4","valueLabel":"PAL4"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-05T14:57:55.953Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141742372-junior-power-sector-analyst","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141742372-junior-power-sector-analyst?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/fa9ad93f-ffb7-4a9d-b501-af2d11b2eb4b?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The International Energy Agency (IEA) is an intergovernmental organisation committed to advancing security of energy supply, economic growth and environmental sustainability through energy policy co-operation. The IEA operates as an autonomous body within the framework of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). The IEA seeks to recruit Junior Power Sector Analysts to contribute to its analytical work on power systems and markets in the Electricity Systems and Markets Division (ESM). The Power Sector Analysts will contribute to the Division’s work on electricity systems and markets, with a particular focus on grids. This includes providing quantitative and qualitative analysis, modelling, and drafting, including for the IEA’s flagship annual Electricity report. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Modelling, analysis and drafting Monitor and analyse technical, regulatory and policy developments in electricity systems and markets at the global, regional and country level. Support the Division’s analytical output on grids, system flexibility and regulation. Contribute to the modelling of the medium-term electricity forecast. This involves the development, operation and maintenance of power sector models. Update and improve relevant technical, regulatory and policy databases on electricity demand, supply and grids (transmission and distribution). Support the end-to-end preparation of the IEA’s Electricity report. Contribute to relevant reports, working papers, presentations and briefing notes for senior management. Collaboration and outreach Support preparations as needed for meetings of IEA standing committees, working parties and other groups as required; participate in relevant meetings of other international organisations; provide support for the development of reports, analyses and information items for these meetings. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background Advanced university degree or PhD in Electrical / Power / Energy Systems Engineering, Energy Economics, Physics or a related discipline. Professional Background A minimum of three years experience of direct power systems work experience in the electricity industry, economic consulting or grid technology companies working on transmission or distribution networks, system operation, energy management and related fields. Strong technical background in power systems and experience working with power utilities and/or grid operators. In-depth understanding of electricity security concepts, power market fundamentals, and the interaction between system operations and market incentives. Solid knowledge of medium- and low-voltage distribution grids, with an understanding of the frameworks governing connection processes and the integration of distributed energy resources. Experience with network planning and operational practices aimed at enhancing the efficiency and utilisation of existing infrastructure is desirable. Experience with power system modelling, such as steady‑state network modelling, dynamic and transient stability modelling, or grid planning and expansion studies, would be an advantage. Proven analytical abilities and excellent writing skills as demonstrated in past work products (analytical reports, quantitative analysis, operative models, and/or published papers). Tools Excellent command of Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel. Solid knowledge of relevant coding languages (e.g. Python, R). Experience with data visualisation tools (e.g. Power BI, Tableau) and database management (SQL) is desirable. Experience with optimisation models and platforms such as Pyomo, PyPSA or GAMS would be an asset. Languages Excellent written and oral command of English, including drafting and proofreading. Knowledge of one or more other working languages would be an asset.
