item.title: Analyste junior du secteur de l’électricité
item.description: {"id":"744000141745339","name":"Analyste junior du secteur de l’électricité","uuid":"5e6c8476-3d80-44c6-93f4-4bb306ae803a","jobId":"f204b628-f7b3-4abf-af0e-b0b5f4e2ad25","jobAdId":"556ed716-3c68-4089-9373-8da09b8d4930","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3349P","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000727","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"5a9445ef-058b-4346-8dca-ef49c8638ded","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL4","valueLabel":"PAL4"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-05T15:03:43.330Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141745339-analyste-junior-du-secteur-de-l-electricite","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141745339-analyste-junior-du-secteur-de-l-electricite?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/5e6c8476-3d80-44c6-93f4-4bb306ae803a?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. L’ Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) est une organisation intergouvernementale qui œuvre en faveur de la sécurité des approvisionnements énergétiques, de la croissance économique et de la durabilité environnementale en promouvant la coopération dans le domaine des politiques énergétiques. L’AIE fonctionne en tant qu’organe autonome au sein de l’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques. L’AIE recherche des analystes juniors du secteur de l’électricité pour contribuer à ses travaux d’analyse sur les systèmes et les marchés de l’électricité au sein de sa Division des systèmes et marchés de l’électricité (ESM). Les personnes retenues prendront part aux travaux de la Division sur les systèmes et marchés de l’électricité et, en particulier, les réseaux. Il s’agira de produire des analyses quantitatives et qualitatives, de réaliser des modélisations et de rédiger des textes, notamment pour le rapport phare annuel de l’AIE consacré à l’électricité. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Modélisation, analyse et rédaction Suivre et analyser les avancées techniques et les évolutions de la réglementation et de l’action publique en lien avec les systèmes et les marchés de l’électricité, aux niveaux mondial, régional et national. Prêter son concours aux travaux d’analyse de la Division sur les réseaux, la flexibilité du système électrique et la réglementation. Contribuer à la réalisation de modélisations en vue d’établir des prévisions à moyen terme relatives à l’électricité : à cet effet, mettre au point, appliquer et actualiser des modèles du secteur de l’électricité. Mettre à jour et améliorer les bases de données pertinentes sur les avancées techniques, la réglementation et l’action publique, qui concernent l’offre et la demande d’électricité ainsi que les réseaux (transport et distribution). Aider à préparer, de bout en bout, le rapport de l’AIE sur l’électricité. Participer à la rédaction de rapports et de documents de travail, et à la préparation d’exposés et de notes de synthèse à l’intention de l’équipe de direction. Collaboration et relations avec l’extérieur Prêter son concours, en tant que de besoin, aux préparatifs des réunions des comités permanents, des groupes de travail et, si nécessaire, d’autres groupes de l’AIE ; participer aux réunions pertinentes d’autres organisations internationales ; concourir à l’établissement des rapports, analyses et éléments d’information destinés à ces réunions. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil idéal Formation Diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur ou doctorat en génie électrique, génie énergétique, génie des systèmes énergétiques, économie de l’énergie, physique ou dans une discipline connexe. Expérience professionnelle Au moins trois ans d’expérience directement acquise sur les systèmes électriques dans une entreprise du secteur de l’électricité, une société de conseil économique ou une entreprise axée sur les technologies de réseau, travaillant sur les réseaux de transport ou de distribution, l’exploitation des systèmes, la gestion de l’énergie ou un domaine connexe. Solide connaissance technique des systèmes électriques et expérience du travail avec des compagnies d’électricité et/ou des gestionnaires de réseau de transport. Compréhension approfondie des concepts liés à la sécurité de l’approvisionnement en électricité, des fondamentaux du marché de l’électricité et de l’interaction entre l’exploitation du système et les incitations du marché. Solide connaissance des réseaux de distribution de moyenne et de basse tension, avec une bonne compréhension des cadres régissant les processus de raccordement et l’intégration des ressources énergétiques décentralisées. Une expérience de la planification du réseau et des pratiques opérationnelles visant à améliorer l’efficience et l’utilisation des infrastructures existantes est souhaitable. Une expérience de la modélisation des systèmes électriques, notamment la modélisation des réseaux en régime stationnaire, en régime dynamique ou en stabilité transitoire, ou de l’étude de la planification ou de l’extension du réseau constituerait un avantage. Capacités d’analyse avérées et excellente compétence rédactionnelle, confirmées par les produits de travaux antérieurs (rapports analytiques, analyses quantitatives, modèles opératoires et/ou textes publiés). Outils Excellente maîtrise des applications Microsoft Office, en particulier d’Excel. Solide connaissance de langages de programmation pertinents (Python ou R, par exemple). Une expérience des outils de visualisation des données (Power BI, Tableau, par exemple) et de la gestion de base de données (SQL) est souhaitable. Une expérience des modèles et des plateformes d’optimisation telles que Pyomo, PyPSA ou GAMS constituerait un atout. Langues Excellente maîtrise de l’anglais à l’écrit et à l’oral, avec des compétences rédactionnelles et éditoriales. La connaissance d’une ou de plusieurs autres langues constituerait un atout. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Informations supplémentaires","text":" Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 2) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 2) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 2) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2). Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de maîtrise 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE . Durée du contrat Durée déterminée de deux ans, avec possibilité de renouvellement. Veuillez noter que, conformément aux Statut et Règlement applicables aux agents de l’Organisation, l’âge de départ obligatoire à la retraite est fixé à 67 ans. Processus de sélection Pour les personnes retenues à l’issue de la présélection, la procédure de recrutement peut comporter l’enregistrement d’un entretien vidéo, une évaluation des compétences professionnelles et un entretien avec un jury. Le présent processus de sélection permettra d’établir une liste de personnes qualifiées que les responsables de l’AIE pourront prendre en considération dans le cadre de futurs recrutements à l’Agence. Les personnes inscrites sur cette liste à l’issue de ce processus de sélection pourront être invitées à des entretiens ultérieurs destinés à permettre l’évaluation de l’adéquation des profils avec des besoins spécifiques. Ces entretiens seront fonction de la spécialisation/du domaine d’intérêt des personnes concernées. Date de clôture Les fonctions décrites ci-dessus seront pourvues dès que possible, et les candidatures devront nous parvenir au plus tard le 14 septembre 2026 à 23h59 (heure de Paris). Ce qu’offre l’OCDE Le salaire mensuel minimum s’élève à 6 008 EUR, plus allocations/indemnités en fonction de la situation personnelle, la rémunération globale étant exonérée d’impôt sur le revenu en France. Cliquez ici pour consulter les Statut, Règlement et Instructions applicables aux agents de l’Organisation. Veuillez noter que tout

item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org. Manufacturing, Agribusiness and Services (MAS) is one of IFC's key industry groups, responsible for a significant portion of IFC's business volume, profitability, and development impact. MAS invests across a diverse range of sectors, including agribusiness, forestry, manufacturing, chemicals, healthcare, education, tourism, property, retail, and other industries, delivering both investment and advisory services through IFC's global network. The MAS Latin America and the Caribbean (MAS LAC) team is seeking a qualified and experienced Associate Investment Officer, or Investment Officer to originate, structure, execute, and supervise investment projects across the region. The selected candidate will play a key role in business development and portfolio management, including restructurings, reschedulings, capital increases, and equity supervision. The candidate should have a demonstrated track record of leading complex investment transactions from origination through commitment and portfolio supervision, preferably across multiple MAS sectors. The position will be based in Guatemala City, Guatemala or San José, Costa Rica. The final duty station and title will be determined based on business needs. Duties and Accountabilities Specific responsibilities include, but are not limited to: • Support or Lead business development efforts across MAS in the country. • Together with the Central America and Caribbean MAS Hub Lead and the WBG country team, lead the scoping and identification process of priority companies to target as IFC clients in the country, considering the strategic areas of focus for MAS in the country. • Actively develop a local network with target companies, financial institutions, financial advisors, and credit agencies in the country. • Lead transaction execution and portfolio management activities across the MAS LAC region. • Evaluate, structure, negotiate, and close new investment transactions, portfolio restructurings, reschedulings, capital increases, equity sales, and other portfolio management activities. • Develop innovative and appropriate financial structures for complex transactions. • Lead or participate in negotiations, leveraging strong financial expertise and influencing skills to achieve successful outcomes. • Work independently and collaborate with senior colleagues to develop a strong pipeline of high-quality investment opportunities in the countries. • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, sponsors, financial institutions, private sector partners, and multilateral organizations to originate new investment opportunities. • Mentor and coach junior investment staff on all aspects of investment processing, portfolio management, and client engagement. • Support dissemination of best practices within the team. • Collaborate closely with Advisory, Environmental Social, Legal, Treasury, and other internal partners to deliver integrated client solutions, manage transaction risks, and maximize development impact. • Collaborate closely with the Upstream team to support market creation efforts and develop a robust pipeline of future investment opportunities. • Collaborate on the preparation of Country Private Sector Diagnostics (CPSD), Country Partnership Framework (CPF), Senior Management Briefs, Country Climate and Development Reports (CCDR), etc. • Engage with World Bank colleagues on MAS-related issues. • Build effective working relationships across multidisciplinary teams and influence internal and external stakeholders to achieve successful transaction outcomes.

item.title: E T Consultant (Regional Engagement Analyst )
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . ITS Vice Presidency Context The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Department Context ITS Operations and Country Engagement Department (ITSOE) delivers innovative products and services to frontline staff working on over 6,000 projects throughout every Region and Global Practice. Our teams support and enable Bank priorities, boost operations efficiency and effectiveness, and facilitate Operational knowledge discovery. Our delivery model leverages global expertise, design and architecture, leading technology, and robust processes to deliver business solutions that ensure value for money. Unit Context The ITS Country Engagement unit (ITSCE) delivers digital support for global and country-specific products, supports systems aligned with the new Country Engagement model, and provides geospatial solutions to improve spatial visibility and impact tracking. It also drives the delivery of AI-powered business solutions to support business priorities and accelerate data-driven decision-making across the institution. The unit’s geospatial portfolio supports operational teams in applying location-based insights, mapping, imagery, and related digital tools to strengthen project design, implementation, monitoring, and communication. The Regional Engagement Analyst serves as a focal point for the ITSCE Solutions. The incumbent supports stakeholder engagement, solution awareness, and adoption across both portfolios, helping country teams, regional teams, and Global Practices identify opportunities where technology, geospatial capabilities, and advisory services can address operational challenges and support development outcomes. Working closely with management, product owners, geospatial specialists, architects, and advisory teams, the coordinator will facilitate engagement, connect stakeholders with relevant expertise and solutions, and help make the ITSCE geospatial portfolio visible, accessible, and relevant across regional, country, and local engagements. The role does not require technical implementation of geospatial solutions but does require sufficient familiarity with available products and geospatial concepts to identify use cases, communicate value propositions, and support adoption. Specific Responsibilities Regional Operations Studio • Serve as the primary point of contact for the Regional Operations Studio and act as an ambassador for ITSOE products, advisory services, and innovation initiatives. • Coordinate Studio activities, ensuring country teams are welcomed, oriented, and connected to appropriate ITSOE products, advisory services, and subject matter experts. • Facilitate workshops, demonstrations, co-design sessions, and engagement activities involving country teams, OPCS, and ITSOE specialists. • Capture and qualify operational needs, technology challenges, and business opportunities and connect stakeholders to the appropriate product, service, or advisory pathway. • Lead outreach, communications, and stakeholder engagement activities to expand awareness, participation, and adoption of the Regional Operations Studio. • Build and maintain relationships with country teams, Regional teams, Global Practices, OPCS, and other stakeholders to strengthen regional engagement and utilization of ITSOE services. • Monitor engagement outcomes and stakeholder feedback to continuously improve the Studio experience and operational impact. Geospatial Solutions Engagement and Adoption • Act as a regional engagement and promotion focal point for the ITSCE Geospatial Solutions portfolio, working closely with product owners and geospatial specialists to identify and advance opportunities with country teams, Regional teams, and Global Practices. • Promote awareness and adoption of geospatial products, services, and advisory capabilities through demonstrations, clinics, roadshows, and targeted outreach activities. • Maintain working knowledge of the ITSCE geospatial portfolio, including project geo-tagging, mapping solutions, imagery-enabled applications, and digital twin use cases, and communicate their operational value in accessible language. • Identify operational challenges that may benefit from geospatial approaches and connect stakeholders with the appropriate product owners, advisors, and technical specialists. • Support the development of presentations, communication materials, demonstrations, and map-based narratives that showcase how geospatial insights can strengthen project design, implementation, monitoring, and decision-making.

The Associate Platform Engineer will support the design, implementation, operation, and continuous improvement of platform engineering and DevSecOps capabilities within the Geospatial Solutions portfolio. Working as the primary DevSecOps resource embedded within the Geospatial Solutions Agile Release Train (ART), the incumbent will be responsible for release management, deployment automation, security remediation, platform operations, and cloud-based solution delivery. The role will support the development and maintenance of scalable, secure, and reliable delivery platforms through the implementation of CI/CD pipelines, Azure DevOps administration, cloud technologies, and operational best practices. The Platform Engineer will collaborate closely with software engineers, product owners, architects, security teams, and business stakeholders to ensure efficient software delivery, operational excellence, compliance with organizational requirements, and continuous improvement across the geospatial solutions ecosystem. Specific Responsibilities • Manage end-to-end release management activities for the Geospatial Solutions portfolio, overseeing the deployment, promotion, and validation of applications and services across development, testing, and production environments. • Design, implement, maintain, and optimize Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines to automate build, testing, security scanning, and deployment processes, enabling reliable, efficient, and secure software releases. • Analyze, identify, and remediate security vulnerabilities across applications, platforms, and environments within the Geospatial Solutions portfolio, supporting secure software delivery and compliance with organizational security requirements. • Administer and maintain Azure DevOps services, including repositories, boards, pipelines, release processes, access controls, and environment management to support Agile software delivery. • Support the deployment, operation, and maintenance of cloud-based solutions and infrastructure across Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services (AWS) environments. • Support containerized application deployments using Docker and related platform (PI) Planning, SAFe Agile ceremonies, and Agile Release Train (ART) activities in coordination with the Release Train Engineer (RTE), contributing to cross-team planning, dependency management, and delivery alignment. • Serve as the primary DevSecOps resource supporting the Geospatial Solutions Agile Release Train (ART), providing technical guidance, operational support, and release coordination across multiple geospatial solution teams. • Collaborate with software engineers, architects, product owners, and platform teams to support solution delivery, operational readiness, and continuous improvement initiatives. • Monitor and troubleshoot deployment processes, DevSecOps workflows, and platform configurations to maintain system reliability, availability, and operational performance. • item.title: Program Officer, Transaction Management
item.description: The World Bank Group Vision and Strategy Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group (WBG) is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 190 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Visit www.worldbank.org . Global Corporate Solutions and Corporate Real Estate Reporting directly to the Managing Director and World Bank Group Chief Administration Officer (MDCAO), Global Corporate Solutions (GCS) brings together the functions of Corporate Security, Corporate Real Estate, and Corporate Services (such as food services, printing, travel, conferences, and translation and interpretation). The World Bank Group’s Real Estate Team (WBGRE) plays a crucial role in supporting the World Bank Group legal entities (IBRD, IFC, IDA, MIGA, and ICSID) by developing and operating their real estate assets worldwide. WBGRE’s primary purpose is to provide safe, cost effective, sustainable, and functional real estate solutions, enabling business units to perform their work program in line with the WBG’s mission to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. To achieve its purpose, WBGRE led by the Senior Manager, is structured into 3 divisions: (i) HQ Real Estate Development Management and (ii) Global Real Estate Development Management and (iii) Global Strategy and Planning or Center of Excellence (CoE). WBGRE also acts as the Secretariat for the WBG’s Real Estate Governance Framework, including supporting the WBG Real Estate Governance process. WBGRE comprises 80+ staff, leverages over 500 contractors, and manages an annual capital investment plan of about $160 million globally. WBGRE works closely with the Bank’s regions managing more than 175 country offices. Job Description The Program Officer, Transaction Management, oversees all aspects of real estate transactions, including purchase and sales inquiries, due diligence, lease reviews and benchmarking, market intelligence, strategy development, vendor and location sourcing, contract and lease negotiations, governance submissions, portfolio management, planning, reporting, and document execution. They provide guidance to internal and external clients, Managers, and senior leadership, ensuring that strategies and transactions are executed seamlessly and aligned with organizational objectives. The position is based Washington DC or Paris and will report to the Manager, International Real Estate GCSF2 (Europe, Central Asia, Latin America, Caribbean) Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: • Support global real estate transactions and their management, including strategy development, market assessment, sourcing, selection, negotiation, and closing and subsequent landlord relationships. • Coordinate acquisition, disposition, expansion, contraction, renewal, termination, and relocation activities across multiple, concurrent projects. Ensure seamless execution through meticulous planning, reporting, and recording. • Coordinate due diligence processes, including property inspections, legal reviews, sellers and lessors’ integrity reviews, and financial assessments • Ensure lease terms and conditions are aligned with the organization’s strategic goals and financial parameters. • Serve as a trusted advisor on commercial real estate, including socio-economic and microeconomic trends, industry developments, workplace strategies, and technological innovations. • Stay informed about market dynamics and corporate real estate advancements. Educate clients and business leaders unfamiliar with industry practices to build organizational capacity. • Collaborate with internal teams (e.g., Legal, Budget, Security) and external stakeholders to ensure sound strategies and decisions. • Actively liaise with landlords and developers to align the World Bank priorities and protect its interests. • Promote awareness of guidelines and drive adherence to real estate governance standards. • Lead transaction controllership and due diligence, coordinating with internal functions and external entities as required to safeguard institutional integrity. • Collaborate with CoE to define in-house versus outsourced tasks, identifying roles, responsibilities, skills, and resource needs for in-house functions. • Collaborate with CoE to Support the engagement of outsourced services and establish the necessary procedures and guidelines for effective process implementation. • Maintain proactive and regular engagement with management, regional team and staff to support transaction planning and management. Note: This vacancy announcement is for one position posted across multiple possible duty stations. That includes Paris and Washington D.C. The selected candidate's duty station will be determined based on organizational requirements and business needs. If the selection is based in Paris, the recruitment type will be local and if the selection is based in Washington DC, the recruitment type will be international

item.title: Senior Transport Specialist – Railways
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank consists of two entities – the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). It is a global development cooperative owned by 189 member countries. As the largest development bank in the world, the World Bank provides loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and coordinates responses to regional and global challenges. For more information, please visit www.worldbank.org . Infrastructure Vertical The WBG Infrastructure Vertical provides public and private solutions to operational teams and clients across the WBG to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs by: (i) supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, (ii) policy environment, and (iii) enabling and mobilizing private sector capital. With 60 years of experience, the WBG is poised to support the sector becoming an engine of growth and jobs through improving policies and governance, foundational infrastructure and private sector investments. The WBG lending in the sector is expected to grow substantially. The Infrastructure VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/infrastructure Transport and Logistics Department Within the Infrastructure VPU, the WBG Transport and Logistics Department seeks to connect people to jobs, social services and income-generating opportunities, as well as to move goods between local, regional, and international markets, using cleaner, safer, more equitable and more resilient transport solutions, with a particular focus on private capital mobilization. The Department is composed of 3 units: (1) Policy and Regulations; (2) Solutions and Impact; and (3) Transport Trust Funds. The Senior Railways Specialist will serve as the department’s senior expert on railways, reporting to the Manager for Transport and Logistics, Policy Regulation. This role will provide thought leadership on railway-related matters; lead the preparation of high-quality knowledge products and advisory services; support regional teams across the World Bank Group in advising on and implementing railway policies, regulations, and solutions; and contribute actively to the Railways Knowledge and Solutions Group. The Specialist will also focus on private sector participation and private capital mobilization in railways and should be proficient in assessing and advising public and private sector partners on business cases and feasibility studies. This vacancy is being advertised for one position across multiple possible duty stations, including Washington, DC, Paris, and London. Key responsibilities: Strategic Leadership and Flagship Research: • Identify key challenges in Railways and initiate solutions and other knowledge initiatives to address these challenges, including new products and financing modalities, with particular attention to private capital mobilization • In partnership with the Global Lead(s) for Railways as well as with regional transport and infrastructure staff, develop a menu of key policy and regulations options that can be used by regional operational/business teams • Formulate strategic directions and associated implementation plan for each upcoming fiscal year and present it to the KTI Management Team for endorsement, as well as mid-year update on implementation of the plan Operational Quality Assurance and Support: • Through the new WBG ADM guidelines, support the quality assurance process across the full lending and ASA project cycle, from upstream support on fundamental design issues to helping extract lessons during the completion process. • Ensure that the most relevant and up-to-date global knowledge informs the design and implementation of country engagements and helps resolve technical disagreements • Extract lessons from WBG operations, curate and disseminate this knowledge across the WBG Learning and Mentoring: • Assess gaps in technical skills based on business needs, and work with the KTI Management Team to internally develop these skills through formal or on-the-job training and through developing a solutions-focused learning curriculum • Support technical staff in deepening their expertise • Regularly convene staff affiliated with the Knowledge and Solutions Group for Railways to discuss emerging issues, share experiences across regions, and identify issues for management attention, ensuring balanced participation of field-based staff along with those based in HQ • Convene field-based friendly training and dissemination events to ensure that best practice experiences are widely known and discussed within the World Bank Group • Identify and promote opportunities for South-South and North-South peer exchange among clients facing similar development challenges Partnership and Outreach: • Build relationships with internal partners to promote effective collaboration across the WBG • Build and nurture existing relationships with external players to forge partnerships, draw on external knowledge and expertise, and support resource mobilization • Represent the World Bank Group in relevant technical meetings, events and partnerships • Participate in the organization of the flagship events (learning week, Transforming Transportation), especially sessions in areas of relevance to the Railways agenda • Act as a public spokesperson for the World Bank Group’s perspective on relevant issues, including conferences, and meetings with partners and civil society • Develop briefings, opinion editorials, blogs, etc. related to emerging opportunities and issues, World Bank Group engagements, and other strategic issues Fundraising and Resource Mobilization: • As part of the department’s fundraising coordination strategy, contribute to the growth of resources and expansion of donors of existing key transport trust funds • Participate in key donor-led events or those organized in collaboration with major donors to enhance visibility of the department’s work

item.title: Senior Energy Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org BACKGROUND South Asia Energy Practice Overview The South Asia Region (SAR) Energy Practice (ISAE1) is part of SAR Infrastructure Group, which also includes the SAR Transport unit and is managed by the Infrastructure Regional Director. One out of four people on the planet live in South Asia, however only one out of 20 units of the world’s power capacity is installed in the region. South Asia has been enjoying rapid economic growth, which is expected to continue strongly after the covid-19 crisis; it is expected to maintain a strongly growing energy demand across countries. While electrification has expanded significantly in the last decade, the power sector continues to have reliability and quality issues, operational inefficiencies, very considerable investment needs, and often challenging financial deficits that impact national budgets. The recent health crisis has affected revenues in the sector and slowed down the rate of infrastructure investments. The South Asia Infrastructure program supports countries in building sustainable, resilient, and inclusive infrastructure systems, while adopting an integrated, cross-sectoral approach to supporting economic growth, job creation, connectivity, resilience, and service delivery across the region. Reflecting the World Bank Group's focus on Private Capital Mobilization (PCM), infrastructure engagements are increasingly developed and implemented in close collaboration with IFC and MIGA, combining public and private sector solutions to maximize development impact. The SAR energy unit contributes to addressing the above challenges with a strong lending and knowledge management work program and a team of about 38 professional staff. The South Asia Energy Program has grown rapidly in the last few years, and has a portfolio of more than US$4 billion, with an annual average lending that usually exceeds US$1 billion. Energy commitments in the region cover reforms (sector and corporate governance, energy security and the environment, utility performance, regional energy exchanges, public-private partnerships, energy efficiency), and investment support in power generation, power and gas transmission and distribution, rural energy electrification, renewable energy development, and low-carbon initiatives. The region is at the forefront of introducing new technologies in energy infrastructure, storage, grids, regional power trade, as well as metals and minerals. Moreover, projects involving natural gas are a key part of delivering energy security for the region and could potentially grow further with future investments in Bangladesh, India, and in other countries. Duties and Accountabilities The SAR Energy Unit of the World Bank seeks a Senior Energy Specialist to support the design and implementation of on-going and future energy sector operations and analytical tasks in the region, with a focus on the gas sector. This position reports to the SAR Energy Practice Manager and the selected candidate will work in coordination with other task team leaders. The responsibilities of the selected candidate will include: The selected candidate will have the following key responsibilities: • Remain up to date with relevant developments globally, and in particular, within the South Asia Region with respect to energy sector, with a focus on natural gas (including gas to power, and transmission and distribution of gas). • Participate in the dialogue with relevant representatives of the private sector to keep abreast of the issues related to the business investment climate and identify possible areas of collaboration through public-private-partnerships. • Contribute to policy dialogue on energy issues and interactions with the client and partners, and alert management to issues requiring attention. • As part of a team, lead/co-lead analytical and strategic work pertaining to energy sector in SAR. • As part of a team, lead/co-lead preparation, appraisal, negotiations and supervision of energy projects. • Coordinate and follow up with government counterparts and consultants, provide high-quality research and analytical support, including drafting policy notes. • Draft and provide timely contributions to project documents, project implementation and project completion reports. • Support the preparation, completion and follow-up of official missions including the drafting of aide memoires and official correspondence. • Other tasks as assigned by the Practice Manager.

item.title: Regional PPP Manager, Africa (North, West and Central Africa)
item.description: IFC — a member of the World Bank Group — is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org . IFC Strategy 2030 sharpens our focus on mobilizing private capital at scale to create more and better jobs, with four building blocks: enhanced origination and mobilization, a differentiated approach to equity, revamped support for MSMEs, and new ways of working that deepen One WBG collaboration. This strategy calls for generating unique opportunities by proactively working “Upstream” to create, deepen, and expand markets and to imagine, design and implement investment projects. It requires taking a systematic approach to understanding the regulatory and sector bottlenecks that prevent the flow of private capital into productive investment in our member countries and addressing these bottlenecks through World Bank Group engagement on policy reforms and programmatic interventions at the country and sector level. IFC is seeking a Regional Manager for Transaction Advisory – PPP to lead its PPP advisory business across North, West and Central Africa. The selected candidate will be based in Cairo, Dakar, Abidjan, or Rabat. Reporting to the relevant Division Directors, the Manager will head a regionally dispersed team, drive business growth, and manage relationships with governments, clients, and key stakeholders. The role also includes oversight support for IFC's Corporate Finance Services (CFS) business in the region. IFC's advisory work covers two streams: PPP Advisory — helping governments design and bring to market commercially robust infrastructure and social services projects — and CFS — providing M A structuring, buy/sell-side services, and capital mobilization support to private sector clients. Key Responsibilities: Strategy and Business Development • Develop and implement regional PPP transaction advisory strategies with Division Directors and Country Managers, prioritizing fragile countries and high-impact projects, and in the context of the World Bank Group private capital mobilization agenda and organizational set-up. • Originate, execute, and manage a pipeline of PPP mandates across infrastructure and public services, ensuring geographic and strategic balance. • Achieve Gross Mobilization targets and regional KPIs; establish impact-focused business and development goals. • Build IFC's market presence and brand in the PPP sector. Team Leadership and Organizational Capacity • Lead, motivate, and develop a high-performing, multicultural regional PPP team. • Build organizational capacity through process, system, and skills improvements. • Contribute actively to Regional Management Teams and collaborate with other CTA Managers on knowledge sharing. Stakeholder Engagement • Cultivate strong relationships with WBG counterparts, governments, sponsors, investors, regulators, donors, and NGOs. • Represent IFC externally and manage diverse stakeholder relationships across the region. Risk and Quality Management • Provide quality assurance on key transaction outputs including due diligence reports, bidding terms of reference, and transaction contracts. • Manage financial and operational risks across the regional PPP portfolio.

item.title: Senior Financial Management Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Governance- Financial Management Unit for East Asia and Pacific (EAP) is recruiting a Senior Financial Management Specialist for Indonesia and Timor Leste country management unit. The selected candidate will bring comprehensive experience in fiduciary risk management, quality assurance, public financial management (PFM), strengthening financial management country systems, policy dialogue, analytical and advisory services and financial management oversight in operations, in addition to strong communication and client engagement skills. East Asia and the Pacific (EAP) Region East Asia and Pacific (EAP) is among the world’s fastest growing, most dynamic regions. The World Bank partners with countries across EAP to promote economic growth and job creation, strengthen human capital, and advance sustainable energy, water, and agriculture for a resilient and prosperous future for all. EAP supports countries focuses on: • Promoting long term growth and jobs by partnering with governments and other stakeholders to shape policies, enable innovation, finance investments, and catalyze private capital • Building human capital and strengthening pandemic preparedness through investments that expand access to education and healthcare • Building resilience by addressing climate risks, reducing pollution, supporting climate smart agriculture, and transitioning to clean and renewable energy East Asia and the Pacific Region: https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/eap Unit Context The Governance -Financial Management (FM) unit (EEAG2), is part of the Prosperity Department in EAP. EEAG2 provides fiduciary assurance services to 22 client countries across seven CMUs. The unit is responsible for the implementation of the Bank’s FM framework for Bank-financed operations, delivering high quality FM services, throughout the project cycle. The Unit also undertakes analytical FM work and country fiduciary assessments. The services provided by the unit include (i) fiduciary assurance; (ii) FM risk management, oversight and monitoring; (iii) quality assurance of FM services; (iv) country portfolio reviews; (v) contributions to country engagement products; (vi) supporting partner countries in enhancing their fiduciary and public financial management systems performance and capacity; (vii) supporting partner countries in developing their professional accountancy institutions, and corporate financial reporting performance (including accounting and auditing standards); (viii) supporting partner countries in developing their internal and external oversight institutions e.g Internal Audit Departments and National Audit Offices. The unit works collaboratively with other departments, global, regional and corporate Bank units. Duties and Accountability The Senior Financial Management Specialist (SFMS) will be based in Jakarta, Indonesia and will be required to support the Bank’s program in Indonesia and Timor Leste and will report to the Practice Manager of the Unit. The SFMS is responsible and accountable providing oversight and quality assurance on operation-level FM support, representing the unit in discussions with the country management unit, taking a proactive role in providing advice and support to clients and for producing agile and innovative approaches to strengthening fiduciary assurance over the use of funds. Leading lending operations in Public Financial Management. Specific duties include: • Assessing the overall adequacy of financial management arrangements and monitoring the FM performance and risks in the pacific lending portfolio; • Providing quality assurance on FM for high risk and complex operations. • Carrying out FM-related risk assessments and proposing appropriate FM arrangements for complex and/or high-risk operations. • providing implementation support and supervising projects financed by loans and grants; • monitoring the implementation of risk mitigation measures and contributing inputs to corporate risk reviews as required; • implementing Bank FM operational systems; • reviewing unaudited interim financial reports, taking appropriate action on any issues arising from the reviews and recommending actions in case of non-compliance; • reviewing audit reports, taking appropriate action on any issues arising from the audits and recommending actions in case of non-compliance; • ensuring compliance with the Bank’s audit and other FM requirements; • ensuring that the project operations are carried out in accordance with sound financial management practices; • providing substantive technical inputs to policy and strategic work on the field of FM, providing inputs to country engagement products and policy and technical notes; • leading the preparation and implementation support for Public Financial Management related lending operations. • leading analytical work on financial accounting, reporting and accountability issues; • leading the provision of FM advice and guidance to the country management unit (CMU) and keep them apprised of key fiduciary issues and provide substantive technical input into policy and strategic work related to country engagement products; • supervising, mentoring and coaching of junior staff and consultants; • carrying out capacity building activities as part of the Institutions team; • supporting partner countries in enhancing their fiduciary systems performance and capacity.

item.title: Lead Digital Specialist
item.description: Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The WBG is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org The East Asia Pacific Region East Asia Pacific (EAP) is a large and diverse region, ranging from Small Island States of the Pacific to the Philippines, Indonesia and China. Despite substantial economic growth and poverty reduction, the EAP region faces huge development challenges. Growth has been uneven across and within countries, institutions still need strengthening, and most countries are heavily affected by climate change. The WBG plays a significant role on global public goods, including climate, biodiversity, water pollution, and health. The World Bank Group is seen as a premier development institution in EAP, with a leadership role on analytical and advisory services as well as financing. East Asia and the Pacific Region: https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/eap Digital AI Vice Presidency Digital technologies offer a unique opportunity to transform development through digital solutions. The Digital and AI Vertical Vice Presidency, and its global and regional teams, support client countries in building their capacities for Digital and AI use. The WBG Digital and AI Vertical is led by a Vice President and was established in July 2024. Our work is anchored in the Digital and AI Strategy, which includes four pillars: access, affordability, ecosystem and AI readiness. The Digital and AI Strategy identifies the priorities that WBG will engage in over the next five years. The Vertical deploys a range of products, services, and partnerships to advance global knowledge across the four pillars of the Strategy through: • Supporting WBG regions that provide financing to governments in the form of grants, loans, guarantees, and risk management products to support digital investment projects and implement policy reforms. • Supporting WBG regions that provide advisory services including targeted policy guidance, technical assistance, and capacity building. • Knowledge products including data and diagnostics to provide actionable insights at regional, country, and local levels, research and thought leadership to expand the global knowledge base, as well as thematic operational toolkits. • Convening services that bring together key stakeholders, from both public and private sectors as well as international and non-governmental organizations involved in advancing global digital transformation. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/digitaldevelopment The Opportunity The WBG engagement in Digital is rapidly growing in the EAP in response to increased client demand for knowledge, technical assistance and financing. The Lead Digital Specialist will lead selected strategic or complex Digital knowledge and operational activities in Indonesia and Timor Leste, coordinate with the ASEAN Secretariat and among ASEAN members on digital issues, and support the delivery of the digital work program across EAP, ensuring technical and operational excellence, and alignment with the Digital and AI Strategy Implementation Plan (FY26–30) and the WBG’s corporate priorities, including the more and better jobs (MBJ) agenda. The Lead Digital Specialist will also play a key role in ensuring that digital activities and initiatives are well-coordinated and integrated across country and regional portfolios in EAP. DUTIES ACCOUNTABILITIES The position is based in Jakarta, Indonesia, and reports to the Practice Manager (PM) for Digital AI for EAP (DEPDU). Key responsibilities include: • Strategic Leadership o In close coordination with the Digital EAP PM, provide technical direction for the Digital AI work program, ensuring alignment with the Digital and AI Strategy Implementation Plan (FY26–30) and EAP regional strategies. o Represent DEPDU in high-level policy dialogues, partnership meetings and regional events, including with the private sector, on Digital and AI. o Connect the mission of DEPDU in delivering on the WBG Digital and AI Strategy Implementation Plan with the efforts of other verticals and sectors, including across the WBG and with IFC and MIGA. o Contribute to the development of partnerships and relationships with external stakeholders, provide technical direction and coordination as part of the WBG’s development partner relationship with the ASEAN Secretariat for digital, and support the effective, timely and relevant reporting of results and impact to donors. • Technical Expertise and Digital Program Delivery o Provide technical leadership to DEPDU teams and client governments on complex digital development issues, including digital and data infrastructure, Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), data governance, cybersecurity, and AI for development. o Lead strategic lending operations. o Work closely with TTLs and country teams to provide guidance, where determined necessary by the Digital EAP PM, on key areas of project design, development, and implementation support and supervision. o Lead the design and implementation of flagship knowledge products for DEPDU, ensuring they are policy-relevant and actionable for client countries. • Operational Support and Mentoring o Guide task teams in integrating the solutions of the World Bank Group’s Global Digital AI Implementation Plan into WBG Lending and Advisory Services and Analytics (ASA) operations across the EAP region. o In close coordination with the Digital EAP PM, review and clear technical deliverables—policy notes, concept notes, mission outputs—to ensure high quality standards and compliance with all corporate requirements, and provide hands-on guidance to task team leaders and client-facing teams on project design and implementation. o Support the Digital EAP PM on portfolio and budget monitoring, anticipating issues and advising the PM on ad hoc issues regarding country engagements (portfolio, sector dialogue), as well as dialogue with country units and partners. o Liaise with global expert teams to provide regional contribution to the Knowledge Bank in alignment with the World Bank Group’s Global Digital AI Strategy; and mobilize support by the Knowledge Bank to regional engagements. o Provide leadership, effective guidance and mentoring, supporting the Digital EAP PM, and serving as a technical adviser to more junior colleagues where needed. • Partnership Management and Outreach o In close coordination with the Digital EAP PM, serve as the focal point in EAP for coordination and engagement with key regional partners, donors and stakeholders active on digital issues. o Facilitate collaboration across the WBG, including between DEPDU, other WBG Global Practices, IFC and MIGA, and EAP CMUs, to ensure the effective transfer of Digital AI knowledge and innovation across sectors. o Provide technical support to colleagues working in other sectors to leverage digital technologies to improve public service delivery and to stimulate digital innovation, entrepreneurship and private sector-led investment. • Results Monitoring, Financial Management and Governance o Ensure effective monitoring, evaluation, and reporting against the Digital and AI Strategy Implementation Plan (FY26–30) Results Framework and workplan indicators for Digital in EAP. o Promote learning, transparency, and knowledge sharing through publications, workshops, and digital platforms.

item.title: E T Consultant – Agile Coach
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 130 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org ITS Vice Presidency Context: The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Unit Context: The IT Transformation Management (TM) function enables ITS to deliver measurable business impact by strengthening how strategy, execution, and performance measurement connect across the organization. TM serves as an integrator across operating model priorities, ensuring ITS modernization efforts contribute to the World Bank Group’s Evolution Roadmap and are supported by clear outcomes, disciplined execution, and transparent performance reporting. The Transformation Office plays a central role in elevating how ITS delivers value by evolving the IT operating model toward greater clarity of ownership, improved value flow, stronger governance, and measurable performance management. This work requires coordinated progress across nine interdependent operating model components: Performance, Organizational Structure, Ways of Working, Tools/Assets, Places, Talent, Sourcing Alliances, Decision Rights, and Financials. This role supports transformation progress—ensuring ITS can continuously improve delivery outcomes while strengthening governance, workforce readiness, and enterprise-wide operating model maturity over time. Duties and Responsibilities: A. Agile Ways of Working Enablement Delivery Coaching • Coach teams and leaders across ITS in adopting and strengthening Agile ways of working, including Scrum, Kanban, and other fit-for-purpose frameworks, adapting practices to team context and maturity. • Facilitate working sessions, team workshops, and leadership discussions to help teams clarify goals, improve collaboration, and accelerate delivery outcomes. • Support teams in establishing effective backlog management, prioritization, and flow practices that improve transparency and predictability. • Identify delivery bottlenecks, coordination challenges, and workflow inefficiencies, and work with teams to implement practical improvements. • Encourage a culture of continuous improvement, helping teams reflect on outcomes and evolve their practices over time. B. Team Formation, Collaboration Ownership Clarity • Support teams in defining clear roles, responsibilities, and ownership models to improve accountability and reduce friction in day-to-day delivery. • Help teams strengthen collaboration across functions and reduce handoffs that slow down delivery. • Facilitate structured conversations that help teams align on ways of working, priorities, and expectations. • Identify areas where organizational structures, processes, or practices create barriers to effective teamwork and propose improvements. C. Execution Visibility, Flow Tooling Practices • Support teams in effectively using enterprise delivery tools (e.g., Azure DevOps) to manage work, improve visibility, and track progress. • Encourage consistent practices around backlog hygiene, workflow management, and delivery tracking to strengthen transparency and accountability. • Help teams interpret delivery metrics and flow indicators to identify opportunities to improve predictability, quality, and delivery speed. • Contribute insights that help leadership understand delivery patterns and systemic impediments. D. Leadership Enablement Continuous Improvement • Partner with leaders and delivery teams to strengthen understanding of Agile principles, team dynamics, and effective collaboration practices. • Facilitate retrospectives, learning sessions, and improvement workshops that help teams evolve their practices. • Provide practical guidance and coaching that helps teams adapt Agile practices to their context while maintaining focus on outcomes and value delivery. E. Stakeholder Engagement Executive Communication • Engage with stakeholders across ITS and the broader WBG community to build understanding of Agile ways of working and how they support the organization’s transformation goals. • Communicate clearly with executive leadership and business partners on how Agile practices improve transparency, collaboration, and value delivery. • Help translate Agile frameworks and delivery practices into clear, mission-oriented narratives that resonate with non-technical audiences. • Support leaders in understanding how Agile adoption strengthens the institution’s ability to deliver outcomes in support of the WBG mission. • Foster open dialogue with stakeholders to address questions, align expectations, and reinforce shared ownership of transformation outcomes.

item.title: Associate Senior Product Owner
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . ITS Vice Presidency Context The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Unit Context The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit supports the World Bank Group’s mission by delivering transformative digital solutions across more than 150 country offices and global locations. Within ITS, the Fiduciary Operations (ITSFD) team, part of Operations Country Engagement Solutions (ITSOE), is leading the modernization of Environmental Social (E S), Procurement, and Financial Management business processes through data, automation, analytics, and Artificial Intelligence (AI). As part of this transformation, ITSFD is implementing an enterprise-scale Agentic AI Platform that leverages cloud-native technologies, Large Language Models (LLMs), multi-agent orchestration, enterprise knowledge retrieval, advanced analytics, intelligent workflow automation, and secure API-driven integration services. The platform is designed to support document intelligence, due diligence, risk assessments, decision support, workflow automation, and conversational experiences across World Bank operations. Position Overview The Associate Senior Product Owner – Operational Financial Management (OFM) leads the strategic vision, backlog prioritization, and execution of next-generation, AI-enabled digital solutions across the institution’s financial management landscape. Operating at the intersection of operational finance, advanced data engineering, and artificial intelligence, this role is responsible for driving the digital transformation of financial governance, fiduciary controls, audit readiness, and financial reporting. The Associate Senior Product Owner translates complex business and financial requirements into scalable AI/ML solutions—including generative AI, intelligent process automation, predictive analytics, and automated anomaly detection—while operating within Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) and Scrum methodologies. Key Responsibilities A. AI Product Vision, Strategy Roadmap • Define and execute an end-to-end product strategy that embeds Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Intelligent Process Automation (IPA) into operational financial workflows. • Align product roadmaps with institutional financial policies, business strategies, and emerging technology trends to automate manual financial processing, enhance financial forecasting, and elevate data accuracy. • Evaluate emerging AI technologies, Generative AI models, and Large Language Model (LLM) orchestration tools for application in financial document processing, intelligent ledger matching, and policy compliance verification. B. AI/ML Backlog Management Agile Execution • Maintain, refine, and prioritize the product backlog for AI-driven financial tools using SAFe and Scrum frameworks. • Translate complex financial operations and machine learning workflows into actionable user stories, feature specs, and technical acceptance criteria tailored to probabilistic model outputs (e.g., accuracy, precision, recall, and acceptable confidence thresholds). • Oversee the end-to-end model delivery lifecycle (MLOps/LLMOps), coordinating training data preparation, model validation, deployment, continuous monitoring, and feedback loops. C. Fiduciary Governance, Responsible AI Compliance Controls • Ensure all AI models and automated workflows strictly adhere to institutional risk management, data privacy, cyber security, and audit standards. • Support development of robust Responsible AI frameworks, focusing on model explainability, bias mitigation, auditable decision trails, and human-in-the-loop (HITL) oversight for OFM transactions. • Partner with internal and external auditors to demonstrate that AI-generated controls, automated reconciliations, and risk scores maintain full compliance and regulatory integrity. D. Core Financial Operations Smart Automation • Support modernization of end-to-end financial management systems working in collaboration with financial management specialists, treasury teams, ITS technical teams, accountants, auditors, and Agile delivery teams • Design AI-driven anomaly detection engines to continuously identify fraudulent activities, duplicate payments, accounting errors, and compliance deviations in real time. • Leverage Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to automate the extraction and validation of unstructured financial data from complex legal agreements, contracts, and financial receipts. E. Data Architecture Infrastructure Alignment • Collaborate with data engineering and enterprise architecture teams to define scalable data pipelines, feature stores, and cloud-based data repositories (e.g., Azure, AWS, Databricks, Snowflake). • Ensure high standards of data governance, lineage, cleanliness, and data readiness required for fine-tuning baseline models and powering enterprise financial analytics. F. Stakeholder Collaboration Change Enablement • Serve as the primary liaison connecting Financial Management Specialists, Accountants, Auditors, Treasury Officers, and Information Technology delivery teams. • Drive change management strategies to promote organizational adoption of AI tools, building trust in machine intelligence through transparent model reporting, intuitive user interfaces, and hands-on training.

item.title: Associate Product Manager
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . ITS Vice Presidency Context The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Department Context The World Bank Group (WBG) is committed to supporting country clients in achieving sustainable development outcomes, including improved health systems, economic growth, education access, climate resilience, and social equity. In this context, digital platforms and data play an increasingly critical role in how development projects are designed, implemented, and adapted. The ITS Operations Products unit (ITSOP) enables digital enablement of the Bank's business processes through a modern, flexible, and user-friendly digital platform that integrates and optimizes critical functions for thousands of front-line staff. It also drives the delivery of AI-powered business solutions to support business priorities and accelerate data-driven decision-making across the institution. To strengthen the feedback loop between the realities on the ground and the digital tools that support operations, ITSOP is seeking a Regional Partner embedded within regional operations. This individual will serve as a trusted advisor to task teams, regional leadership, and product teams in identifying opportunities to optimize operations through fit-for-purpose technology solutions and smarter business processes. As the organization accelerates its adoption of emerging technologies to support development goals, the Regional Partner will play a critical role in identifying, analyzing, and promoting innovative solutions that enhance business processes, service delivery, and knowledge management. Responsibilities A. Eliciting Business Requirements • Engage with business stakeholders to understand product requirements and goals; synthesize needs, pain points, and opportunities across the Financing domain. • Direct market and user research to inform hypotheses to be tested in product strategy; incorporate user feedback and analytics to validate and refine requirements. B. Managing the Product Roadmap • Define and communicate the product strategy, roadmap, and overall vision; ensure alignment with ITS/WBG priorities and client outcomes. • Drive product decisions by balancing business value, operational risk, compliance requirements, technical feasibility, and user experience considerations • Identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and operational efficiency across the financing lifecycle. • Lead collaboration with the Agile Release Train to ensure timely and successful delivery of the product roadmap and continuous value delivery. • Design clear governance structures for the product (decision rights, roles, cadences) and ensure compliance with WBG governance policies and standards. • Balance new investments, enhancements, and technical debt to maximize value and manage risk. C. Stakeholder Engagement • Facilitate stakeholder communication to identify opportunities for improvements to the product roadmap and vision; build consensus across business and technical teams. • Serve as primary point of contact for the product; communicate roadmap, status, risks/issues, and outcomes to leadership and user groups. • Oversee vendor relationships (as applicable) to ensure resource availability, scope/quality adherence, and successful product vision delivery. D. Financial Management and Performance • Propose strategic investments to support product development and manage technical debt; prepare inputs for governance and funding decisions. • Monitor the financial management of the product to ensure budget availability and adherence to WBG processes. Official Use Only • Define and track success metrics (OKRs/KPIs) for outcomes, adoption, reliability, and operational efficiency; guide prioritization using evidence and analytics. • Monitor product operational health and support volumes; drive actions that improve user value and reduce total cost of ownership.
