item.title: E T Temporary
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank consists of two entities – the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). It is a global development cooperative owned by 189 member countries. As the largest development bank in the world, the World Bank provides loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and coordinates responses to regional and global challenges. Visit http://www.worldbank.org/ Regional Context The Middle East and North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan Region serves twenty two countries across different income groups, of which fourteen are active/potentially active IBRD/IDA borrowers (Afghanistan, Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Pakistan, Syria, West Bank and Gaza, Tunisia, and Yemen), with a total of 251 projects and over $51 bn in total commitment. Eight are users of the Region's non-lending services, mostly on a reimbursable basis (Bahrain, Kuwait, Libya, Malta, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates). The mission of the region is to foster sustainable growth with a focus on job creation and poverty reduction, economic and social inclusion, and good governance. The region attaches importance to creating a supportive work environment based on the values of teamwork, transparency, trust, and client service, underlined by professional excellence. The region places high value on diversity. The region is organized into seven Country Departments (CMUs), the Office of the Regional Chief Economist, and the Development Effectiveness Unit (MNADE). With an expanded regional strategy, the World Bank aims to help the region weather the current crises, move from stabilization to transformation, unlock its vast economic potential of youth and women, develop its human capital to adapt to global megatrends, and foster innovation ( https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/mena ). Djibouti is one of the smallest countries in Africa, with an area of 23,200 square kilometers and a population estimated at about 990,000. The size of its economy limits its ability to diversify production and increases its reliance on foreign markets, making it more vulnerable to market downturns and hampering its access to external capital. With less than 1,000 square kilometers of arable land (0.04% of its total land area) and average annual rainfall of only 130 millimeters, Djibouti depends almost completely on imports to meet its food needs. As of June 2026, Djibouti’s active portfolio comprised 17 IDA projects worth about US$501 million. The portfolio is focused on energy, transport, digital transformation, education, health, social safety nets, energy, rural community development, slums upgrading and urban poverty reduction, governance, and private sector development, with an emphasis on women and youth. For more information on Djibouti, please visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/djibouti Roles Responsibilities: The Extended Term Temporary (ETT) will perform several functions, including, but not limited to: Main Tasks: Resource Management: • Serve as the primary liaison for vendors, assisting them with any inquiries related to their payments. • Facilitate the identification of accrual amounts and ensure timely follow-up with vendors to secure prompt submission of invoices. • Support the creation of purchases orders and registration of vendors • Document all relevant supporting elements for adequate RM monitoring • Monitor and report on resource usage • Coordinate with various GPs and team members to ensure efficient use of charge codes, supporting documents • Liaise with the RM team based in Cairo and other relevant units to ensure CO satisfactory score card Support to Global Practices: • Assist the GPs with administrative, mission and logistical support • Handles mission planning and preparation • Schedule and coordinate meetings, appointments, and travel arrangements with external stakeholders/clients • Prepare and distribute meeting agendas, minutes, and other relevant documents • Maintain and organize files, records, and documentation • Support the GPs in their day-to-day activities and tasks during the missions • Offer administrative support to the office in facilities, administration, procurement, and finance as need be • Assist with recruitment processes and coordinate logistics for high-level visits, as need be • Other tasks (back up program assistant in case of absence of main program assistant)

item.title: ET Consultant
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 130 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org ITS Vice Presidency Context: The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w The World Bank Group has undertaken an ambitious exercise to revise its mandate, products, and structure to adjust to the multiple, intertwined crises affecting the world today (see Evolution Roadmap). In the move to a better bank, a new Vision and Mission for the institution have been announced, and a new World Bank playbook along with several financial initiatives are underway. Background: The WBG Library provides services to about 24,000 WBG staff and consultants globally. The unit provides access to e-resources, reference and research services, training, and custom solutions. The team is decentralized to serve a mobile, global workforce from HQ, Asia, Europe, and Africa. The Library is looking for a dynamic, experienced Research Librarian to provide research and reference services to support the business. The Library is a unit of ITS Data, Information AI Products Services (ITSDA), within the WBG Data Technology Office (ITSDO), part of the Information Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidency. ITSDO provides information services to the World Bank Group and to the public. The WBG Library is also part of the Library Network, a group of libraries supporting World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund staff globally. WBG Library is an institutional member of NISO and IFLA and participates in The United Nations Library Information Network for Knowledge Sharing (UN-LINKS) and UNSEIAC Consortium. Position Details The WBG Library seeks an experienced, service-oriented, and collaborative ETC Research Librarian to support research, reference, document delivery, market intelligence, systematic literature review, and AI-enabled research services. The role will help strengthen the Library’s ability to deliver timely, high-quality research support to WBG staff in HQ and Country Offices, while contributing to emerging work on AI for research and information integrity. The ETC Research Librarian will work with Research team members, support front desk reference services, and collaborate with other WBG IT teams and internal and external Library partners to deliver on the WBG Library Research mandate. Scope of Work The ETC Research Librarian will support the following areas: A. Research and Reference Services Conduct in-depth research covering development sectors, investment industries, and other priority areas relevant to World Bank Group operations. Respond to research and reference requests from Library clients in HQ and Country Offices within defined service level expectations. Provide high-quality reference and document delivery support, including Ready Reference services and front desk coverage as required. Use academic search engines, Open Access resources, and relevant information tools to support client research requests. B. Research Products and Knowledge Support Prepare research outputs, reports, literature scans, and evidence summaries to support WBG staff and operational teams. Conduct or support systematic literature reviews and structured evidence searches. Create and publish topical research guides aligned with WBG knowledge priorities and knowledge verticals. Contribute to WBG’s body of knowledge for internal and/or external client solutions. C. AI for Research and Information Integrity Support AI for Research activities, including the evaluation and validation of AI-generated information, data, and research outputs. Assist staff in assessing the reliability, relevance, and quality of information used in WBG projects, investments, and knowledge work. Contribute to development of reusable prompts, prompt chains, or other practical approaches that support effective research strategies using emerging technologies. D. Data, Analytics, and Reporting Provide regular reports and statistical analysis to the Library Research Team Lead. Support data analysis and visualization activities for internal decision-making and service improvement. Support business insights from research services, including use of APIs where relevant to research needs. Respond to company and financial market data-related questions using relevant tools such as Capital IQ and similar resources. E. Collaboration, Client Engagement, and Service Support Work effectively as part of the Library Research team and collaborate with Content and Access Management, Outreach and Promotions, ITS, ITSDO, and other internal stakeholders. Collaborate with external partners to identify and provide relevant information that supports WBG business priorities and client country capacity building. Present and train others on Library services and resources when required. Test or pilot library-related products and provide user feedback to improve services. F. Systems, Policies, and Operational Support Use the Library Case Management System to receive, create, manage, and respond to client requests. Participate in day-to-day development and maintenance of information resources and services. Contribute to the formulation and implementation of Library policies, standards, guidelines, and procedures. Apply knowledge of copyright, intellectual property, and ethical use of information in fulfilling client information requests. Expected Deliverables The ETC Research Librarian will be expected to deliver: 1. High-quality research responses, literature reviews, reference outputs, and document delivery services within agreed service levels. 2. Research guides, knowledge products, evidence summaries, and topical resource materials aligned with WBG knowledge priorities. 3. Support for AI-enabled research, including validation of AI-generated information and development of practical research support approaches. 4. Regular reporting, statistical analysis, and insights on research service activity and client demand. 5. Contributions to client training, peer learning, product testing, and knowledge sharing across the Library and relevant ITS/ITSDO teams.

item.title: Program Analyst
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . VPU Context: The World Bank Group’s (WBG) Ethics and Internal Justice Services Vice Presidency (EIJ) brings together, under a single umbrella, the WBG’s approach to values, ethics and the resolution of workplace conflict. EIJ’s vision is to foster a values-based workplace culture and help staff uphold the WBG’s ethical standards. EIJ provides an integrated, empathetic and efficient approach to resolving workplace conflict, allowing staff to focus with urgency on the WBG’s mission. EIJ’s work covers each of the five WBG institutions. https://www.worldbank.org/en/about/unit/ethics-and-internal-justice-services Unit Context: The incumbent will play a key role in managing the RWA learning sessions, coordinating the delivery of the RWA “Case of the Month” and developing program content, preparing reports and communications materials, and supporting overall program administration. The successful candidate will have demonstrated experience in project and learning event management, preferably within a conflict resolution or related environment. Strong analytical, communication, organizational, and stakeholder engagement skills are essential. The role requires sound judgment, professionalism, discretion, and the ability to work effectively in a multicultural and highly confidential environment. The Program Analyst will report to the Head of EIJCS and will be based at the WBG Headquarters in Washington, DC. Duties and Responsibilities: · Design, coordinate, deliver, and track monthly learning sessions for RWAs across multiple time zones. · Lead the development and enhancement of innovative learning experiences including micro-learning, scenario-based content, including the “Case of the Month” initiative, based on identified RWA learning needs. · Support the preparation and delivery of learning programs and workshops with practitioners, ensuring high-quality participant experience and effective coordination. · Design and administer structured survey instruments and contribute to learning analytics by synthesizing participant feedback into actionable summaries. · Undertake additional assignments and provide back-up support functions as required by the Head of EIJ Client Services.

item.title: Platform Engineer (SAP BW and Data Platforms)
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 130 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org ITS Vice Presidency Context The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Unit Context The ITS Financial Technology (ITSFT) unit enables critical Finance and Accounting functions through enterprise platforms supporting financial management, accounting, budgeting, reporting, analytics, external reporting, trust fund management, lending operations, and institutional performance management. The unit manages and modernizes enterprise data and analytics platforms including SAP BW, SAP Business Objects, Azure-based data platforms, and reporting solutions while supporting strategic initiatives related to data modernization, cloud adoption, operational reporting, compliance, and financial transparency. Duties and Accountabilities Role Purpose The Platform Engineer (SAP BW Data Platform) is responsible for the engineering, administration, modernization, and operational excellence of the World Bank Group's enterprise analytics and data platforms. The role supports SAP BW on HANA, Business Objects, SAP data integration technologies, Azure-based data platforms, and enterprise reporting solutions. The Platform Engineer collaborates with product owners, architects, data engineers, business stakeholders, and infrastructure teams to ensure platform reliability, performance, scalability, security, governance, and continuous improvement. The position contributes to the evolution of enterprise analytics capabilities through automation, modernization initiatives, cloud adoption, DevOps practices, observability, and platform engineering principles, enabling trusted and timely business insights across financial and operational domains. Key Responsibilities SAP BW Platform Engineering • Administer, maintain, and optimize SAP BW on HANA environments. • Manage platform upgrades, patches, transport, performance tuning, and capacity planning. • Support business-critical financial and operational reporting processes. • Ensure platform availability, resiliency, scalability, and operational stability. • Support BW upgrade, modernization and migration initiatives, including cloud and next-generation analytics platforms. • Perform professional-level analysis and platform engineering activities across data and analytics platforms. • Solve moderately complex platforms, integration, performance, and operational challenges. • Collaborate with business and technology stakeholders to define solutions and drive continuous improvement. • Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing within the platform engineering and analytics delivery teams. • Apply practical expertise across data platforms, analytics architecture, cloud technologies, integration, security, and operational support. Integration Data Operations • Manage SAP BW, SAP ECC, SAP BODS, and related enterprise data integrations. • Support incident response, root cause analysis, and issue remediation activities. • Collaborate with upstream and downstream application teams to ensure reliable data movement and processing. • Monitor platform health, data loads, and integration performance. Analytics Reporting Platforms • Support Business Objects, Power BI, Bex, Analysis for Office and enterprise reporting solutions. • Ensure reporting platform performance, reliability, and operational excellence. • Partner with business stakeholders to enable trusted, timely, and scalable reporting capabilities. Security, Risk Compliance • Ensure compliance with World Bank security, audit, data governance, and operational risk requirements. • Support security reviews, vulnerability remediation, and platform hardening activities. • Participate in audit response and compliance remediation efforts. • Maintain appropriate controls for access management, data protection, and system integrity. Agile Delivery Collaboration • Participate in SAFe Agile ceremonies including PI Planning, Iteration Planning, Reviews, and Retrospectives. • Collaborate with Product Owners, Architects, Scrum Masters, and Engineering teams to prioritize platform improvements. • Contribute to backlog refinement and technical roadmap planning. • Support continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives.

item.title: E T Consultant (Communication and Engagement)
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 130 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org ITS Vice Presidency Context The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Department Context ITS Operations and Country Engagement Department (ITSOE) delivers innovative products and services to frontline staff working on over 6,000 projects throughout every Region and Global Practice. Our teams support and enable Bank priorities, boost operations efficiency and effectiveness, and facilitate Operational knowledge discovery. Our delivery model leverages global expertise, design and architecture, leading technology, and robust processes to deliver business solutions that ensure value for money. Unit Context The ITS Country Engagement unit (ITSCE) delivers digital support for global and country-specific products, supports systems aligned with the new Country Engagement model, and provides geospatial solutions to improve spatial visibility and impact tracking. It also drives the delivery of AI-powered business solutions to support business priorities and accelerate data-driven decision-making across the institution. The unit’s geospatial portfolio supports operational teams in applying location-based insights, mapping, imagery, and related digital tools to strengthen project design, implementation, monitoring, and communication. The Communication and Engagement officer supports ITSCE unit in communications, stakeholder engagement, and business coordination. Develops executive communications, manages outreach activities, coordinates events and engagement opportunities, and helps increase awareness and adoption of ITSCE priorities, solutions, and services. Works closely with leadership, product teams, internal and external business stakeholders to deliver clear, consistent messaging, support strategic initiatives, and strengthen collaboration across the Bank, and partner organizations. Translates complex topics into concise business messages and ensures effective execution of leadership priorities through strong coordination and communication. Specific Responsibilities • Serve as a focal point for ITSCE communications, stakeholder engagement, and business coordination activities. • Prepare presentations, briefing notes, talking points, leadership updates, newsletters and announcements. • Develop success stories, adoption stories, impact narratives, and promotional materials highlighting ITSCE solutions and initiatives. • Coordinate communications and engagement activities with Regions, Global Practices, OPCS, DEC, other ITS teams, MDBs and external partners. • Manage stakeholder interactions and build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, track follow-up actions and support the timely execution of leadership priorities communications and engagement activities. • Coordinate and help organize workshops, forums, roadshows, and other internal and external events, including agendas, materials, communications, and stakeholder coordination. • Facilitate information flow between leadership, product teams, business stakeholders, and partner organizations. • Maintain stakeholder engagement plans, communications calendars, and tracking mechanisms. • Monitor engagement outcomes, stakeholder feedback, and communication effectiveness and prepare management reports and summaries. • Identify opportunities to increase awareness, sponsorship, adoption, and visibility of ITSCE products, services, and strategic initiatives. • Support preparation of management reviews, strategic planning activities, and executive engagement materials.

item.title: Deputy Chief Executive Officer, GPE
item.description: The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and 182 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org VPU Context: The Global Partnership for Education (GPE) is a shared commitment to end the world’s learning crisis. It is the only global partnership and fund dedicated entirely to helping children in lower-income countries get a quality education, so they can unlock their potential and contribute to building a better world. We bring together governments, teachers, civil society, donors, United Nations agencies, development banks, businesses and private foundations to transform education systems so that every girl and boy can have hope, opportunity and agency. What We Do GPE helps low- and lower-middle-income countries build stronger education systems so that all children can get the education they need to thrive. We support more than 90 countries where the needs are greatest and focus on reaching the children who are the most vulnerable, including girls, children with disabilities, and those affected by extreme poverty or conflict. Our unique approach works. Between 2021 and 2025, GPE supported 372 million children in partner countries to get a better education through grants and co-financing. How We Work GPE is working to help governments transform their education systems to get the most vulnerable children in school, improve teaching and learning, and build equitable, inclusive and resilient education systems fit for the 21st century. Transforming education is about creating lasting changes and achieving impact on a scale. GPE sets out to deliver this transformative change by convening partners, mobilizing funds and catalyzing reforms to help partner countries accelerate access, learning outcomes and gender equality. Multiply Possibility – Financing GPE 2030 GPE launched its 5th financing campaign for 2026-2030, co-hosted by Italy and Nigeria, to mobilize $5 billion for inclusive, high-performing education systems in the world’s most challenging contexts. This funding will unlock $15 billion in total education investment through co-financing and multiplier effects. A fully funded GPE will transform education systems and multiply possibility for 750 million children in 96 countries. Governance And Organizational Arrangements The GPE Board of Directors includes ministerial-level board members and alternates representing 20 constituencies that reflect the partnership’s breadth. The Board Chair is H.E. President Jakaya Kikwete and the Board Vice Chair is Ms. Christine Hogan. The Board of Directors, with its standing committees, provides policy and strategic oversight and approves or delegates funding decisions. The GPE Secretariat, with 160 employees and hosted by the World Bank, is responsible for translating the policies and strategies set by the Board into practical support for partner countries, coordinating with diverse stakeholders and galvanizing global support for SDG 4. The Secretariat’s headquarters are in the World Bank’s offices in Washington, D.C., with a European office in Paris, an African office in Nairobi, a satellite office in Brussels, and a support office in Chennai. ABOUT THE JOB Description The Deputy Chief Executive Officer (DCEO) reports to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and shares with the CEO responsibility for leading, managing and representing GPE. The role sits between strategy and execution, translating Board direction and CEO vision into a functioning, coordinated system across a complex partnership model. The DCEO is accountable for making the system work end-to-end, ensuring countries, grant agents, and partners operate coherently, and turning strategy into results. The DCEO directly supervises all managers, including the COO, CFO and CTO, who oversee the full breadth of GPE operations. The DCEO also serves as the manager of the Executive Office and the Governance Team that supports the Board of Directors. The DCEO is an ex-officio member of the Board of Directors and the Board’s Executive Committee. The DCEO represents GPE in various international fora, coordinates high level relationships, and manages a diverse body of work. He/she also oversees the GPE management team and is responsible for ensuring organizational coherence. Duties And Accountabilities Provide Strategic and policy direction: •With the CEO, helps shape and approve strategic direction and policy development. •Advises strategic, policy and operational matters before the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee. •Under GPE2030, ensures programs and organizational units are aligned with and maximizes the impact of the three strategic objectives on education reform, finance and partnership. •Champions gender equality and inclusion in all aspects of GPE’s work. Represent GPE to external audiences and partners: •Represents GPE in international fora, including the Sherpa committee of the SDG4 High-level Steering Committee •Engages with senior government officials of donor and partner countries, and leadership in INGOs, foundations and private firms. •Provides leadership to GPE’s efforts to raise critical resources for the GPE Fund and for co-financing. Lead Secretariat operations: •Oversees the breadth of Secretariat functions and operations related to regional/country programs, governance, personnel and organizational development, finance and grants, external relations, evaluation, monitoring and data management. •Ensures internal alignment, cross-team coordination, clear workflows, and efficient processes. •Oversees and drives efforts to improve the coherence, efficiency and cost-effectiveness of Secretariat operations. Manage Corporate Governance: •Manages the governance team •Manages governance operations related to the Board of Directors and its committees. •Supports and advises the Chair and Vice Chair in their Board duties. •Ensures the Secretariat provides strategic, high-quality and timely documentation to facilitate Board and committee deliberations. •Supports the Vice Chair in their role as Chair of the Executive Committee. Oversees portfolio performance and delivery: •Ensures the grant portfolio is on track, and corrective action is taken as needed. Ensures quality and timeliness of partnership compacts, grant applications, and implementation progress. Intervenes when programs stall; grant agents underperform or country processes break down. Orchestrates the GPE operating model: •Ensures clarity on roles, decision rights and escalation pathways. •Encourages partner alignment behind country priorities •Ensures coherence across funding windows •Strengthens the effectiveness of the model by reducing fragmentation, improving clarity and efficiency, and reducing competing incentives. Oversee results, data, and performance management: •Holds partners accountable for delivery timelines, quality of implementation, results reporting. •Ensures strong monitoring frameworks, reliable data flows from countries and grant agents, and performance tracking across the portfolio. •Provides data and reporting to shape Board discussions and make strategic adjustments. Manage risks: •Identifies and mitigates political risk, operational risk, governance risk, financial risk, PSEAH and reputational risks to GPE.

item.title: Data Scientist
item.description: Main Responsibilities Data Infrastructure Development and Management Design, develop and maintain automated data pipelines (backend and frontend) for the OECD How’s Life? well-being database on the OECD Data Explorer, ensuring robust quality assurance processes Manage regular data updates (at least quarterly) for the How’s Life? database and the Better Life Index. Coordinate the data collection process for the Committee on Statistics and Statistical Policy, including drafting requests and engaging with national statistical offices Stay abreast of emerging data science and AI tools and methods, and assess their potential application to well-being data infrastructure, visualisation and analysis Data visualization and design for policy impact Maintenance and further development of the OECD Well-being Data Monitor, the WISE Centre’s interactive well-being data hub, including front-end design, integration with the Data Explorer backend, and alignment with the OECD’s web architecture Create compelling and accessible data visualisations to enhance the visibility and uptake of WISE Centre outputs among policy makers and other stakeholder groups, ensuring scalability across knowledge products Closely collaborate with the WISE communications team and other OECD communications units as needed Capacity building and internal knowledge sharing Engage with relevant communities of practice within the OECD’s data science network to share expertise and contribute to innovation Provide training and technical guidance to the WISE team on best practices in data science, automation, and data visualization Well-being policy analysis and reporting Analysis and drafting for selected WISE statistical and policy publications related to well-being topics. Examples might include the How’s Life? flagship report, well-being country studies, and topical reports on issues such as identifying policy factors for happy, healthy and connected ageing across OECD countries Analyse well-being outcomes using statistical techniques, including econometric modelling and microdata analysis, across economic, social, and environmental domains., and identify trends that merit policy attention in the context of rapidly evolving economic, ecological, digital and demographic transitions Present findings and policy implications to internal and external stakeholders, including national governments and international partners Project management, supported by the Head of Unit, of the analysis, drafting and publication process of these WISE knowledge products
item.dc:creator: OECD

item.title: Expert(e) en science des données
item.description: Responsabilités principales Développement et gestion de l’infrastructure de données Élaborer, développer et tenir à jour des pipelines de données automatisés (back-end et front-end) à l’appui de la base de données Comment va la vie ? dédiée au bien-être sur l’Explorateur des données de l’OCDE, en veillant à la robustesse des processus d’assurance qualité. Gérer les mises à jour régulières (chaque trimestre au moins) de la base de données Comment va la vie ? et de l’Indicateur du vivre mieux. Coordonner la collecte de données pour le Comité des statistiques et de la politique statistique, notamment en rédigeant des demandes et en collaborant avec des offices statistiques nationaux. Se tenir informé(e) des nouveaux outils et méthodes dans les domaines de la science des données et de l’IA, et évaluer s’ils pourraient être appliqués à l’infrastructure, à la visualisation et à l’analyse de données sur le bien-être. Visualisation et conception de données à fort impact sur l’action publique Assurer la maintenance et poursuivre le développement de l’Observatoire des données sur le bien-être de l’OCDE, le portail interactif de données sur le bien-être du Centre WISE, y compris le développement frontal, l’intégration avec la partie back-end de l’Explorateur de données, et l’alignement sur l’architecture web de l’OCDE. Créer des visualisations de données convaincantes et accessibles en vue d’améliorer la visibilité et l’adoption des produits du Centre WISE auprès des responsables de l’action publique et d’autres parties prenantes, en assurant l’évolutivité des produits fondés sur les connaissances. Collaborer étroitement avec l’équipe de communication du Centre WISE et d’autres unités de communication de l’OCDE, selon les besoins. Renforcement des capacités et partage des connaissances en interne Dialoguer avec les communautés de pratique compétentes au sein du réseau de l’OCDE sur la science des données afin de mettre en commun les compétences et de contribuer à l’innovation. Dispenser des formations et des conseils techniques à l’équipe de WISE quant aux meilleures pratiques en matière de science des données, d’automatisation et de visualisation des données. Analyse des politiques relatives au bien-être et établissement de rapports Analyses et rédaction dans le cadre de certaines publications statistiques et stratégiques du Centre WISE ayant trait au bien-être, notamment le rapport phare Comment va la vie ?, les études par pays sur le bien-être, et les rapports thématiques sur certaines questions comme les leviers de l’action publique permettant d’assurer un vieillissement épanoui, en bonne santé et riche en liens sociaux dans les pays de l’OCDE. Analyser les résultats en matière de bien-être au moyen de techniques statistiques, notamment la modélisation économétrique et l’analyse de microdonnées, dans les domaines économique, social et environnemental, et repérer les tendances qui méritent l’attention des pouvoirs publics dans le contexte de l’évolution rapide des transitions économique, écologique, numérique et démographique. Présenter les conclusions et les implications pour l’action publique aux parties prenantes internes et externes, comme les administrations nationales et les partenaires internationaux. Avec l’appui de la Cheffe de l’Unité, superviser le processus d’analyse, de rédaction et de publication des produits de WISE fondés sur les connaissances.

item.title: E T Consultant - Real Estate Decarbonization Consultant
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Infrastructure Vertical The WBG Infrastructure Vertical provides public and private solutions to operational teams and clients across the WBG to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs by: (i) supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, (ii) policy environment, and (iii) enabling and mobilizing private sector capital. With 60 years of experience, the WBG is poised to support the sector becoming an engine of growth and jobs through improving policies and governance, foundational infrastructure and private sector investments. The WBG lending in the sector is expected to grow substantially. The Infrastructure VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/infrastructure Please note this position is financed by a Trust Fund and renewal is contingent upon availability of funding, in addition to other factors, including but not limited to business needs, staff performance and skills fit. This vacancy announcement is for one position posted across multiple possible duty stations. That includes New Delhi, India and Washington DC. The selected candidate's duty station will be determined based on organizational requirements and business needs. Job Duties and Responsibilities: The ET Consultant’s (ETC) primary role will be to support Industry Specialists in technical due diligence of potential and on-going real estate decarbonization projects. Working closely with IFC’s Industry Specialists, IFC’s contracted consulting firm(s), and client/client’s local consultant(s), the ETC will either lead or provide support in the following areas for Decarbonizing Real Estate for Impact and Value Enhancement (DRIVE) projects: • Assess sustainability strategies to identify gaps and areas of improvement • Evaluate energy efficiency, energy storage, building electrification and renewable measures to assess their feasibility for DRIVE projects • Conduct and/or review baseline assessments for real estate portfolio emissions • Provide recommendations to determine clear climate goals (net-zero by 2050, etc.) in line with international frameworks, such as Science Based Target Initiative (SBTi) • Provide recommendations on the decarbonization strategy and pathway prepared for DRIVE • Recommend strategies to reduce greenhouse emissions and energy, water and material consumption for real estate portfolios • Review CapEx plans for the portfolio to meet required targets, savings, and payback period • Research new regulations in relevant markets that would impact the business operations and valuations for Clients • Review strategies for maximizing on-site/off-site renewable energy options • Review framework for monitoring and reporting on the progress of the implementation of DRIVE client’s decarbonization roadmap • Other related tasks, as needed
item.dc:creator: World Bank Group

item.title: E T Consultant for Digital Health Transformation-Kenya
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . Eastern and Southern Africa (AFE) Region We need the best and brightest talent focused on our region in order to harness the potential and innovation happening across the continent. Home to about 700 million of Africa’s people, Eastern and Southern Africa is a geographically, culturally and economically diverse region of 26 countries stretching from the Red Sea in the North to the Cape of Good Hope in the South. The subregion harbors some of Africa’s protracted conflicts, rendering many of its countries fragile, while significant gaps in education, health, and skills development continues to keep people from reaching their full potential. This creates a huge development challenge, impacts heavily on the lives and livelihoods of people, and hinders regional integration and trade. But it also creates an opportunity to work closely with country leaders, civil society, development partners, and young people to chart a brighter course for the future. We are looking for dedicated professionals to join our innovative and diverse team to improve people’s lives. Health, Nutrition and Population (HNP) Global Practice Context: The central contribution of the HNP Global Practice to the World Bank’s twin goals is to enable the achievement of Universal Health Coverage (UHC), in which all people are effectively covered by essential health services, and nobody suffers undue financial hardship because of illnesses. The HNP Global Practice includes staff members in Washington, DC and many country offices. The HNP Global Practice works with and across multiple sectors, in recognition of the fact that HNP outcomes often depend on actions that lie outside the HNP sector. The HNP Global Practice supports country and regional efforts to: (i) improve health outcomes, especially for the poor and most vulnerable; (ii) expand access to high-quality HNP services, interventions and technologies that give the most value for money; (iii) strengthen health systems for results; (iv) establish and improve health financing mechanisms that promote efficiency, equity and sustainability of investments; (v) strengthen health-relevant institutions within and outside the health sector; (vi) harness multisectoral policies and investments for better health outcomes; and (vii) develop and learn from rigorous impact evaluations. Eastern and Southern African Region Digital Health and Country Context Africa's health systems stand at a genuine inflection point in digital health. Across the Africa East (AFE) region, there is a genuine opportunity to leapfrog older, incremental digitization pathways by building diagnostic tools, administrative systems, and AI-enabled platforms directly on newer digital rails such as mobile connectivity and cloud infrastructure. The World Bank is supporting the digitization of countries' healthcare systems and prioritizing improved access to essential health services. This is being done through various lending operations and technical assistance in the post-COVID era. Kenya In order to build an interconnected and secure digital ecosystem to support Universal Health Coverage (UHC), the Government of Kenya enacted the Digital Health Act and established a Digital Health Authority (DHA) with the mandate to lead the country's digital health transformation agenda. DHA’s core responsibilities include developing and managing a Comprehensive Integrated Health Information System that allows for real-time health information exchange across public and private health facilities; establishing unified national registries for patients, health facilities, healthcare workers, and medical products; serving as the national regulatory authority for all digital health solutions; and ensuring data sovereignty. This institutional structure gave Kenya's Ministry of Health the stewardship mechanism required to coordinate investments and pursue transformation at national scale. Democratic Republic of the Congo In the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), a comprehensive national digital health information system remains at an early stage of development. Nevertheless, the Government has already launched a number of digital transformation initiatives aimed at improving access to and the quality of healthcare service delivery across the country. Currently, the national health information system is primarily anchored on the District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2) platform and relies on routine data collected which combines paper-based reporting mechanisms from local health facilities through intermediate levels up to the Ministry of Public Health. In response to growing demand for more efficient, data-driven health services, the Government has embarked on an ambitious health digitalization agenda. As part of this effort, the Ministry of Public Health established the National Agency for Clinical Engineering and Health Digitalization (ANICNS), which has developed a national digital health master plan currently under implementation. The strategy is founded on key pillars including interoperability of health systems, homologation digital health solutions, strengthened governance frameworks, and infrastructure. A central objective of this initiative is to progressively connect health facilities nationwide to DHIS2, thereby enhancing health data collection, management, analysis, and utilization. Rwanda In Rwanda, the Health Intelligence Center (HIC) functions as a national strategic platform that gathers, processes, and analyzes real-time health data drawn from across the entire healthcare system. It integrates inputs from a wide range of sources, including the DHIS2 health management information system, electronic medical records (through e-Ubuzima and cEMR), civil registration and vital statistics, logistics management (eLMIS), population health tracking (WelTel), emergency medical services, and health workforce data. Using a six-layer digital architecture and artificial intelligence, the HIC supports disease surveillance, early outbreak warning, resource allocation, and evidence-based policymaking, and it has been recognized internationally as a model for embedding AI into national health governance. The e-Ubuzima (eBuzima) initiative is the locally developed electronic medical records platform that feeds directly into the HIC and forms the operational backbone of Rwanda's push toward full health system digitization by the end of 2025. It synchronizes patient records across public health facilities, giving both patients and providers real-time access to medical history, which helps reduce waiting times, ease hospital congestion, and improve prescription accuracy. Much more is needed to further improve the interoperability of various data sources and to enhance evidence-based, timely decision-making at various levels. Uganda Uganda has made major progress in digital health, moving from a fragmented, pilot-heavy “e-chaos” environment toward a more coordinated national system. Key foundations include the National eHealth Policy (2016), eHealth Strategy (2017), and the National Digital Transformation Roadmap 2023/24–2027/28. DHIS2 remains the backbone of the national health information system, supporting routine data use across more than 7,000 facilities. Spatial connectivity gaps, staff turnover, limited data-analytics capacity, and continued paper-based reporting still affect data quality, use, and leverage of digital systems. Uganda’s digital health agenda is now aligned with NDP IV, Vision 2040, and the national health compact. A new generation Digital Health Strategy is under preparation to support national health policy objectives at a time technologies like Machine Learning and AI promise to elevate digital capabilities from traditional resources and information management system to direct service delivery levers. The country is more determined to achieve interoperability across various information and digital systems in the next 5 years. Overall, the country is seeking to shift from donor-supported pilots to sustainable, nationally owned, and financially resilient digital health systems. Duties and Accountabilities The ETC will support digital health transformation across country operations by providing technical assistance on strategy, governance, interoperability, data use, responsible AI, capacity building, and implementation of practical solutions that strengthen health systems and improve service delivery. Digital Health Strategy, Policy, and Operations • Lead and contribute to technical assistance and lending operations that help countries design, prioritize, implement, and scale digital health solutions to improve service delivery, data governance, use, and transparency, aligned with national health priorities and UHC objectives. • Advise client countries and World Bank teams on policy, legal, institutional, procurement, and governance reforms for digital health transformation, including responsible AI, data governance, privacy, cybersecurity, and vendor management. • Provide strategic advice to governments, World Bank teams, and relevant stakeholders on digital health reforms, platforms, technologies, and investments that improve system quality, efficiency, transparency, equity, sustainability, and impact, drawing on global good practice, country context, capacity, and portfolio needs. • Conduct analytical work, including desk reviews, key informant interviews, and field visits, t

item.title: Senior Transport Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org Europe and Central Asia Region The Europe and Central Asia Region (ECA) is seeking a Senior Transport Specialist for the Transport unit (IECT1) within the INFRA Practice Group, who will report to the Practice Manager and be based in Washington DC. The Europe and Central Asia (ECA) region comprises 30 extremely diverse countries, with a population of nearly 500 million people. Three of our client countries are IDA only and another two are IDA blend countries. The remaining 25 are IBRD eligible. Although ten of our clients have joined the European Union and seven of these have graduated from IBRD, most continue to remain active recipients of knowledge and/or financing through the WBG’s lending services. ECA has a strong lending pipeline as well as a large and growing portfolio of Reimbursable Advisory Services. Knowledge is critical to the World Bank’s value proposition to client countries in the ECA region in both lending and advisory services. A predominantly middle- and high-income region, ECA continues to be at the forefront in confronting the numerous development challenges that countries face in the evolving global economy. The region is at the vanguard of building regional connectivity while having to manage the changing structure of the labor market. At the same time, digital technologies are changing the nature of work, populations are aging, and large migration flows have generated social tensions that have contributed to increased political polarization. More recently, the invasion of Ukraine and its aftermath threaten to reverse the region’s achievements in regional integration, poverty reduction and shared prosperity. Transport Global Practice Better transport has the potential to improve the lives and livelihoods of billions of people by facilitating access to jobs, markets, and essential services such as healthcare or education. The World Bank provides financial and technical assistance to help countries implement sustainable mobility solutions that create real, lasting development benefits. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/transport The ECA Transport Unit (IECT1) The ECA Transport Unit (IECT1) has an active portfolio of 21 lending operations with total commitments of about USD5 billion, 10 ongoing ASA and reimbursable advisory services (RAS) and approximately 2-4 new lending deliveries per FY. The current portfolio is diversified which reflects different client needs, with the following development objectives: (i) improving regional connectivity to enhance trade opportunities through regional integration and efficient freight logistics, enhancing national connectivity and urban mobility to support more inclusive urban development; (ii) strengthening the capacity of clients to plan and implement transport interventions across transport modes through policy and institutional reforms, improving the knowledge-base and feedback loops, strengthening planning processes, managing environmental and social safeguards and mainstreaming social accountability; (iii) leveraging resources through strong partnerships (donor coordination and PPPs), including increasing commercial and domestic financing for connectivity, mobility and logistics projects in the countries, and (iv) ensuring sustainability by improving governance and efficiency in the sector, bringing transformative technologies on transport planning and service delivery, and increasing resilience of transport infrastructure and supporting a low carbon path. The position in Washington DC will primarily cover road sector initiatives across the region. The IECTR unit is looking to recruit a seasoned senior road sector specialist with a solid track record in policy dialogue, business development, and implementation of operations in the road sector, demonstrated through strong track record in the areas among road sector institutional reform, investments (experience with guarantee instruments would be a big plus) and experience with implementing rated criteria in transport sector investments. First hand experience working directly in road agencies at provincial/national levels would be particularly valued for this position. Role Responsibilities: The chosen candidate will be part of a team responsible for: (i) implementation of the road sector program in the region, which includes RAS’s on sector reform, investment projects increasing with a focus on sector reform and bringing commercial financing into the sector; (ii) leading the technical dialogue (advisory and analytics) in the road sector with the authorities in ECA countries; (iii) identifying new opportunities and preparing new projects in the region; (iv) leading policy/institutional reforms and mainstreaming key initiatives on incorporation of the private sector; logistics, transport sector reform and resilience (v) developing analytical and advisory work and knowledge activities in close collaboration with other Global Practices, leveraging on best practices, international experiences and innovative tools and data analytics; and (vi) in all above activities, contribute to maximizing private sector financing by partnering with IFC/MIGA/WB World Bank Infrastructure Finance and Guarantees Units. The specific duties will include leadership of and support to project preparation, supervision, analytical studies consistent with the World Bank’s sector strategies, with a particular focus on: • Expertise with the use of rated criteria in investments and their application in WB transport investment projects. The ideal candidate would have in depth and practical experience with rated criteria design and implementation in settings that have experience with quality based contracting. • Leading the development of road sector strategies with a focus on road sector institutions, and governance and public-private partnerships. • Funding and financing innovations in the road sector and bringing commercial financing into the road sector. • Leading the day-to-day implementation of active projects in countries in the regions, including lending and non-lending operations • Identifying and developing a pipeline of project and programs in ECA countries in accordance with the country strategies, especially where private capital mobilization is envisioned. • Advising government counterparts on technical matters associated with transport projects, including on institutional strengthening activities, technical designs and specifications, compliance with environmental and social policies, procurement, operational health and safety, etc. • Supporting the World Bank-wide professional community of staff engaged in the transport practice by participating in a selected number of Solution Areas under the Transport Global Solutions Groups, delivering technical notes to enhance the creation and dissemination of new knowledge, and expanding the existing knowledge base. • Staying abreast of recent developments in the transport sector world-wide, and on cross-cutting issues, in relation to the topics of specialization for this position; identifying knowledge gaps and disseminating relevant knowledge to clients. • Delivering high quality transport projects in general, through high quality project documents, state of the art technical advice, and strong focus on quality assurance.

item.title: Statistician – Development Finance
item.description: Main Responsibilities Policy analysis and advice Contribute to the drafting of documents, presentations, reports, and web products containing statistical data. Prepare high quality accurate data and statistics for working papers and publications, including the OECD Development Co-operation Report. Contribute to methodological work on development finance statistics, particularly on ODA eligibility assessments. Data management Contribute to the development of innovative data frameworks that include automated data management processes, data exchange and validation with a large group of participating institutions, and data accessibility to the public. Contribute to the production and maintenance of development finance datasets published by the DCD. Improve the presentation of development finance statistics by preparing graphs, tables, maps, and developing dynamic dashboards and other data visualisation tools. Meeting support and facilitation Contribute to the organisation of meetings and workshops and capacity-building events on ODA reporting. Prepare presentations and briefing materials as required. Provide communication support to the Division teams on key messages and story-telling in the area of development finance. Other tasks Contribute to joint projects and activities with other sections of DCD, the OECD or other key partners. Carry out other related duties, as assigned. Support data analysis and visualisation for the DAC Review, as requested.
item.dc:creator: OECD

item.title: Statisticien·ne - Financement du développement
item.description: Responsabilités principales Analyse des politiques et conseils Prendre part à la rédaction de documents, d’exposés, de rapports et de produits web contenant des données statistiques. Préparer des données et statistiques exactes de grande qualité destinées aux documents de travail et aux publications, notamment au rapport Coopération pour le développement . Contribuer aux travaux méthodologiques sur les statistiques du financement du développement, en particulier sur les évaluations de l’éligibilité à l’APD. Gestion de données Contribuer à l’élaboration de cadres innovants pour les données, qui portent notamment sur des processus de gestion automatisée des données, sur l’échange et la validation des données avec un vaste groupe d’institutions participantes, et sur l’accessibilité des données pour le public. Contribuer à la production et à la maintenance des ensembles de données sur le financement du développement publiés par la DCD. Améliorer la présentation des statistiques portant sur le financement du développement, par la préparation de graphiques, tableaux et cartes, ainsi que par l’élaboration de tableaux de bord dynamiques et d’autres outils de visualisation des données. Appui aux réunions et facilitation Contribuer à l’organisation de réunions et d’ateliers ainsi que d’événements consacrés au renforcement des capacités concernant la notification de l’APD. Préparer des présentations et des notes de synthèse en tant que de besoin. Fournir à la Division un soutien à la communication concernant les messages clés et la mise en récit dans le domaine du financement du développement. Autres tâches Apporter sa contribution à des projets et activités menés conjointement avec d’autres sections de la DCD, de l’OCDE ou d’autres partenaires clés. Accomplissement d’autres tâches connexes conformément aux instructions données. Contribuer à l’analyse et à la visualisation des données pour le Processus de révision du CAD, conformément aux instructions données.
item.dc:creator: OECD

item.title: The Nuclear Energy Agency - Software Engineer
item.description: Main Responsibilities Software Infrastructure Development Modernise the CPS Workflow: develop a secure, efficient software and database infrastructure to streamline code and benchmark distribution. Work with NEA colleagues to ensure the effective integration of new software into broader NEA IT infrastructure and facilitate logging and reporting of CPS distribution activities. Maintain and monitor relevant Data Bank digital services, interfaces and associated infrastructure, applying modern best practices in all areas of your work, including the re-implementation of functionality from legacy codebases to other programming languages while ensuring consistency of business logic and system behaviour. Assist senior staff with the implementation and maintenance of new API-enabled frameworks for the management of nuclear physics data, nuclear energy experimental data, and other data, as required. Communication and Liaison Develop good working relationships and close contacts across the Agency and Data Bank to understand software and database needs across the business and act as a contact point for scientific software solutions. Work closely with Data Bank staff to understand user needs and advise on software and DevOps solutions. Report on and present the work of the NEA Data Bank in your area of work to internal and external audiences. Other Carry out other related duties as assigned by the Head of the Data Bank.
item.dc:creator: OECD

item.title: L’Agence pour l’énergie nucléaire - Ingénieur(e) logiciel
item.description: Responsabilités principales Développement de l’infrastructure logicielle Moderniser le flux de travail du CPS : développer une infrastructure logicielle et de bases de données sécurisée et efficace afin de rationaliser la distribution des codes et des benchmarks. Travailler avec les collègues de l’AEN afin d’assurer l’intégration efficace des nouveaux logiciels dans l’infrastructure informatique plus large de l’AEN et de faciliter la journalisation et le reporting des activités de distribution du CPS. Maintenir et surveiller les services numériques, interfaces et infrastructures associées pertinents de la Banque de données, en appliquant les meilleures pratiques modernes dans tous les domaines de travail, y compris la réimplémentation de fonctionnalités issues d’anciens codes dans d’autres langages de programmation, tout en garantissant la cohérence de la logique métier et du comportement du système. Aider le personnel senior à mettre en œuvre et à maintenir de nouveaux cadres activés par API pour la gestion des données de physique nucléaire, des données expérimentales relatives à l’énergie nucléaire et d’autres données, selon les besoins. Communication et liaison Développer de bonnes relations de travail et des contacts étroits au sein de l’Agence et de la Banque de données afin de comprendre les besoins en matière de logiciels et de bases de données dans l’ensemble des activités, et agir comme point de contact pour les solutions logicielles scientifiques. Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le personnel de la Banque de données afin de comprendre les besoins des utilisateurs et de conseiller sur les solutions logicielles et DevOps. Rendre compte et présenter les travaux de la Banque de données de l’AEN dans votre domaine de travail à des publics internes et externes. Autres Exécuter toute autre tâche connexe confiée par le/la Chef(fe) de la Banque de données.
item.dc:creator: OECD

item.title: E T Consultant (Data Analyst)
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 130 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org ITS Vice Presidency Context: The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Role purpose: The Data Analyst is responsible for analyzing data assets to support organizational decision-making. With guidance, this role assists in the design and execution of data analytics initiatives, supports collaboration with stakeholders, and supports the development of statistical models, predictive models and machine learning techniques to solve complex business problems. Key Responsibilities: Analytics Integration 1. Supports analytical services or operational work in core areas of data science. 2. Assists with the development of a data governance framework that includes clear guidelines for data classification, ownership, and stewardship. 3. Leverages statistical concepts, practice, and theory, and knowledge of probabilities to support stakeholders in identifying key operational issues and optional solutions. Solutions Design and Implementation 1. Supports the delivery of data, research and evidence-based solutions for institutional directions and strategic vision. 2. Collaborates to develop data solutions and market knowledge and ensure continuous processes improvements. 3. Assists with the development of data models and manages data processing and cleaning, supporting quality assurance and data visualization. 4. Supports the development of machine learning and AI tools to accelerate reasoning and analysis to support decision making. Business Analysis: 1. Collects and documents business requirements, including establishing acceptance and evaluation criteria 2. Defines configuration specifications and business requirements to ensure alignment with roadmap objectives Agile: 1. Helps teams self-organize, self-manage, and deliver via effective SAFe Agile methods 2. Assist in the preparation process for PI planning, and drafts PI plans in coordination with the Agile team 3. Tracks team progress and utilize metrics to identify areas for enhancement Communication and Narrative 1. Help translate technical analyses in core areas of data science into recommendations for programs, policies, and strategies for social and economic development. 2. Supports the adoption and suggestion of new concepts and ideas to from inside and outside the organization to optimize data solutions.
item.dc:creator: World Bank Group
